location_raw: District Dadu, District Larkana, or SIOVS Hyderabad
job_description:
Position Vacant
We are one of the leading non-profit organizations in Pakistan that’re working towards improving health, promoting education, alleviating poverty, building infrastructure, and developing social institutions for community empowerment. Our aim is to empower the poor. HANDS strength is 14 volunteer board members, 10,000 work force and thousands of community-based volunteers of more than 6,300 partner organizations.
HANDS requires following staff for HANDS DO’s Dadu and Larkana
Position: Optometrists
No. of Positions: 03 (01 for Dadu & 02 for Larkan)
Place of Posting: Dadu / Larkana / SIOVS – Hyderabad
Age Limit: 25-45 Years
Reporting Line: Project Manager SIOVS
Qualification: Optometrist
Experience: At least 2 years of clinical experience
Skills: Clinical skills
Terms of References for Optometrists:
1. Background
HANDS Welfare Foundation in collaboration with CBM International and with the technical support of Sindh Institute of Ophthalmology and Visual Sciences (SIOVS) Hyderabad, under project “Improving Access to Inclusive Education and Healthcare in Rural Sindh”, aims to strengthen access to primary eye care services for underserved populations in Dadu and Larkana. To support this initiative, the services of qualified Optometrists are required to conduct comprehensive vision assessments, deliver community outreach services, and contribute to early detection, prevention, and management of eye health concerns within the community in the target project areas.
2. Objective of the Assignment
The primary objective of the Optometrist’s assignment is to deliver high-quality clinical and community-based eye care services, aligned with the standards of the World Council of Optometry (WCO), and to support the effective implementation of HANDS’/SIOVS eye health program through screening, diagnosis, referral, and awareness raising.
3. Scope of Work
A. Clinical Services
Conduct comprehensive eye examinations, including refraction, cycloplegic refraction, and advanced refraction for all age groups.
Performing low vision assessments and prescribing appropriate low-vision aids.
Prescribing and fitting hard and soft contact lenses.
Conducting advanced visual function assessments (e.g., binocular vision, accommodation tests).
Detecting, diagnosing, and referring ocular diseases and abnormalities to ophthalmologists/specialists as needed.
Using slit lamp bio-microscopy and applanation tonometry proficiently
Ensure accurate patient record management and compliance with clinical protocols.
Ensure adherence to infection control, sterilization, and patient safety guidelines.
Ensure proper counseling on eye conditions, spectacles use, and follow-up care
B. Community Eye Health Activities
Participate in school screening and community-based eye screening according to the project work plan.
Collaborate with Social Organizers to ensure efficient team functioning and community mobilization and outreach.
Provide training and capacity building to LHVs, LHWs, teachers, and basic project staff on vision testing and eye health promotion.
Support awareness activities promoting six healthy signs of the eye and eye health practices.
Serve as an active and cooperative team member during field and outreach operations.
C. Data Management & Reporting
Maintain complete, accurate, and timely clinical and screening records.
Assist in data collection, entry, organization, and basic analysis as per project requirements.
Uphold data confidentiality and ethical handling practices.
Prepare and submit weekly, monthly, and ad-hoc activity reports to the Project Manager.
Contribute data for Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability, and Learning (MEAL) processes.
D. Research & Program Support
Participate in operational or field research activities related to eye health, as assigned.
Support the planning, organization, and implementation of eye camps and community outreach events.
Contribute to monitoring, evaluation, and quality improvement of program activities.
4. Accountability
The Optometrist will report directly to the Project Manager.
When posted at RHC, THQ, or DHQ, the Optometrist will also remain accountable to the Medical Superintendent of the respective facility.
Compliance with HANDS policies, professional ethics, and field discipline is mandatory.
Participate in routine staff meetings, supervisory sessions, trainings, and performance reviews as required.
5. Deliverables
Weekly and monthly clinical and screening activity reports submitted on time.
Accurate documentation of patient records, referrals, and follow-up outcomes.
Active participation in all scheduled outreach events, screenings, and program activities.
Training sessions conducted for community and project staff (if required).
Contribution to research data and findings, when applicable.
Compliance with defined quality and performance standards of the project.
6. Required Competencies
Strong clinical skills in refraction, ocular assessment, diagnostic and patient management
Proficiency in slit lamp bio-microscopy and applanation tonometry.
Ability to work effectively in both facility-based and community settings.
Strong communication, teamwork, and interpersonal skills.
Ability to conduct training and capacity-building activities.
Competency in data management, reporting, and use of basic digital tools.
Commitment to community eye health and willingness to travel frequently within project areas.
7. Duration and Location
This is a project-based assignment. The Optometrist will be stationed in District Dadu, District Larkana, or SIOVS Hyderabad, with frequent travel to field sites, schools, screening venues, and rural communities as required by the program.

And also candidates can submit CV’s at: Sindh Institute of Ophthalmology & Visual Sciences (SIOVS) @ Eye Hospital, Journalist Society, Hyderabad, Sindh Pakistan.

job_title: Business Planning Specialist
job_description:
Duty Station: Lahore (with field travel across project districts)
Reporting To: Project/Marketing Specialist / Team Lead
Employment Type: Project-based / Contractual
Project Background
The PRIAT Project aims to strengthen agricultural value chains, improve market access, promote crop diversification, and increase farmer incomes and resilience across selected districts of Punjab. A key project intervention is supporting Farmer Enterprise Groups (FEGs) to establish viable small and medium agro-processing and value-addition enterprises (e.g., dehydration units, cold storage, packing houses) through sound business planning, feasibility assessment, and access to grant financing.
Role Purpose
The Business Planning Specialist will be responsible for developing high-quality, bankable business plans and pre-feasibility studies for FEGs and small/medium producer enterprises applying for PRIAT project support. This includes market analysis, technical and process design inputs, financial planning, costing, and risk assessment, culminating in comprehensive, investment-ready business plans in line with project formats and donor requirements.
The position will work closely with the Marketing Specialist, technical teams, and field staff to gather primary and secondary data, validate assumptions, and produce business plans that support FEGs in accessing grant financing and achieving commercial viability.
Key Responsibilities
Business Plan Development
Prepare comprehensive, bankable business plans/pre-feasibility studies for FEGs and small and medium producer enterprises (e.g., dehydration units, cold storage, processing/packing units) under the PRIAT Project.
Develop structured business plan content including executive summary, background and rationale, market analysis, proposed business model, product mix, process flow, and marketing strategy.
Ensure business plans are tailored to the specific value chain, enterprise type, and target market (domestic and export).
Market and Financial Analysis
Conduct market analysis including demand trends, competitor comparison, pricing, and market linkage opportunities (domestic and export).
Develop financial projections, including project cost estimates, equipment and setup costs, production costs, and expected sales revenue.
Assess the profitability and viability of the proposed enterprise, including how much profit is expected and how long it will take to recover the investment.
Prepare financial statements/annexures such as profit & loss, cash flow, and balance sheet projections, along with key assumptions used.
Assess raw material requirements, value chain and logistics gaps, and human resource needs for proposed enterprises.
Technical and Risk Inputs
Coordinate with technical specialists to incorporate machinery, equipment, and process specifications into business plans.
Conduct risk analysis (commodity-associated and socio-economic) and propose mitigation measures.
Ensure business plans address regulatory compliance, quality standards, and certification requirements relevant to the enterprise/value chain.
Grant Financing and Capacity Building Support
Develop grant disbursement plans and financing mechanisms in line with project subsidy ceilings and applicant financial allocation guidelines.
Support FEGs and producers in understanding business plan content and financial projections as part of capacity building.
Prepare detailed action plans and implementation timelines for proposed enterprises.
Coordination and Reporting
Liaise with FEGs, field teams, and the Marketing Specialist to gather accurate baseline production, cost, and market data.
Ensure business plans meet project formats, donor requirements, and quality standards prior to submission for review/approval.
Maintain organized documentation and records of all business plans developed.
Qualifications & Experience
Master's degree in Business, Economics, Finance, or a related discipline.
Minimum 7 years or more of general experience in his/her field of expertise.
Proven specific experience in business planning, business modeling, or a related field for small and medium producers/enterprises.
Experience developing feasibility studies or business plans involving market analysis, financial planning, and costing is essential.
Experience in the agriculture/agri-processing sector and familiarity with Punjab's value chains will be preferred.
Proficiency in MS Excel is required.
Skills & Attributes
Strong analytical and financial planning skills.
Excellent business writing and report presentation skills.
Sound understanding of market analysis, costing, and investment assessment.
Ability to translate technical and field data into clear, structured, and investment-ready business plans.
Strong coordination skills to work with cross-functional teams and field staff.
Ability to manage multiple business plan assignments within tight timelines.
Willingness to undertake field travel across project districts as required.
Key Performance Indicators
Number and quality of business plans/feasibility studies completed within agreed timelines.
Accuracy and soundness of financial projections.
Approval rate of submitted business plans against project/donor quality standards.
Timeliness of coordination with FEGs, field teams, and technical specialists in data collection.
Quality and completeness of documentation for each business plan developed.

job_title: PN 33 - Ongoing Recruitment: STTA - Junior Level National - Research Associate – Digital Learning & Coordination Support
job_description:
E4H Punjab TOR - TA for Developing e-Certification Programme on MSDS Capacity Building for Healthcare Providers
Programme
Evidence for Health (E4H) is a Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO)-funded programme aimed at strengthening Pakistan's healthcare system, thereby decreasing the burden of illness and saving lives. E4H (2023-2027) provides technical assistance (TA) to Punjab and also to the Federal and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) governments. The Punjab component is being implemented by Palladium along with Oxford Policy Management (OPM).
Through its flexible, embedded, and demand-driven model, E4H Punjab will support the government to achieve a resilient health system that is prepared for health emergencies, responsive to the latest evidence, and delivers equitable, quality, and efficient healthcare services. Specifically, E4H will deliver TA across three outputs:
Output 1: Strengthened integrated health security, with a focus on preparing and responding to health emergencies, including pandemics.
Output 2: Strengthened evidence-based decision-making to drive health sector performance and accountability.
Output 3: Improved implementation of Universal Health Coverage, with a focus on ending preventable deaths.
E4H-Punjab works in partnership with the Punjab Department of Health (DOH).
Terms of reference
Background
Under Sections 13–20 of the Punjab Healthcare Commission (PHCC) Act of 2010, PHCC is mandated to regulate healthcare establishments (HCEs) across Punjab through registration, licensing, and quality assurance functions. Over the past decade, PHCC has implemented a range of capacity-building initiatives to support HCEs in effective Minimum Service Delivery Standards (MSDS) implementation, including online learning modalities and specific certification programmes.
Since 2010, PHCC has implemented multiple physician engagement initiatives to drive MSDS uptake. These include: 1) Free of cost orientation sessions; 2) on-site MSDS orientation sessions for HCEs; 3) Desk review and coaching through implementation cell; 4) The 2024 Hospital Infection Prevention & Control e-certification module, which saw 68% completion rates among targeted Cat-II/III hospital staff; and 5) District-level Continuing Medical Education sessions on quality standards, with emphasis on PHC. These approaches have increased physician familiarity with MSDS requirements and created demand for structured learning, as evidenced by HIPC module uptake. The proposed e-certification expands this model to remaining nine MSDS functional areas.
PHCC’s current digital learning platform hosts the HIPC e-certification module and supports:
User self-registration and profile management for physicians/administrators
Bilingual content delivery with video, PDFs, and quizzes
Automated tracking of completion and certification issuance
Basic analytics dashboard for PHCC administrators.
The platform is web-based and mobile-responsive, with negligible licensing cost to end-users. Utilisation data from HIPC shows >5800 registered users and
While MSDS implementation remains variable, the constraints extend beyond regulatory requirements and include limited awareness, managerial challenges, and competing operational priorities. In this context, there is a need to strengthen structured and accessible learning pathways that can support consistent understanding and application of MSDS.
Globally, healthcare regulators are increasingly complementing oversight functions with structured digital learning approaches to support continuous professional development (CPD) and quality improvement. While such models provide useful reference points, PHCC’s experience indicates that incremental adaptation of existing approaches, rather than the introduction of fully new systems, is both appropriate and feasible.
Building on the experience of the HIPC module, and emerging global healthcare regulatory trends, the PHCC has identified an opportunity to expand its existing e-certification programme to cover the remaining nine MSDS functional areas. The proposed Technical Assistance (TA) is therefore intended to support progressive expansion and refinement of this approach, in alignment with PHCC’s regulatory mandate. The MSDS functional areas to be covered under this TA include:
Access, Assessment and Continuity of Care (AAC)
Care of Patients (COP)
Patients’ Rights and Education (PRE)
Management of Medication (MOM)
Continuous Quality Improvement (CQI)
Facility Management and Safety (FMS)
Responsibilities of Management (ROM)
Human Resource Management (HRM)
Information Management Systems (IMS)
Problem Statement
Despite the availability of a comprehensive MSDS framework, its effective implementation across the HCEs remains uneven. While PHCC has undertaken focused capacity-building initiatives to address this challenge, the efforts have not been successful for system-wide competency development. These gaps are particularly evident in primary healthcare facilities, where variability in provider competencies and limited access to structured training mechanisms affect standardisation, continuity of care, and quality outcomes.
In this context, expanding e-certification to the 9 additional MSDS functional areas can contribute to:
improved understanding of MSDS
consistent application of quality requirements
strengthened CPD pathways
The TA is therefore intended to support the structured expansion and refinement of PHCC’s existing e-certification approach, ensuring that learning content, delivery mechanisms, and certification processes remain practical and scalable in principle.
Goal and Objective(s)
Goal
To support PHCC in strengthening implementation of MSDS and improving quality of healthcare including primary healthcare delivery in Punjab by building provider competencies through a scalable e-certification approach across all functional areas, using its current digital learning systems.
Objectives
To develop and integrate structured e-certification modules for the remaining nine MSDS functional areas.
To strengthen utilisation of existing PHCC digital learning platform for course delivery, assessment, and certification processes.
To support institutionalisation of the e-certification approach through iterative user feedback, and development of basic governance and content management processes.
Expected outcome:
The e-certification programme is expected to contribute to healthcare strengthening including PHC through:
Improved provider competency in core MSDS areas
Increased adherence to MSDS during PHCC inspections
Enhanced patient safety culture in primary care settings.
For PHC facilities, key outcomes include better triage, referral, and infection control. For Cat-I/II/hospitals, outcomes include improved clinical governance and medication safety. The programme applies equally to public and private HCEs, supporting uniform quality standards across Punjab’s mixed health system. Impact will be tracked via pilot pre/post assessments and LMS completion analytics.
Strategic Approach
The TA supports PHCC’s ongoing efforts to complement its regulatory functions with practical learning approaches, aimed at improving understanding and application of MSDS across HCEs. The programme will explicitly support primary healthcare strengthening by targeting first-contact care providers. Course content will incorporate principles of people-centred care, continuity of care, referral linkages, patient rights, safety, and equitable access, particularly for underserved populations. Building on PHCC’s existing experience with the HIPC e-certification module, the TA focuses on translating MSDS requirements into structured and accessible learning formats, enabling professionals to more effectively interpret and apply standards within routine service delivery.
The approach is designed to incrementally strengthen healthcare worker capacity and support more consistent implementation of quality standards.
In addition, the use of existing digital platforms provides an opportunity to improve accessibility of learning resources across different types and locations of healthcare establishments, while supporting PHCC in establishing practical, scalable mechanisms for continuous professional development.
Scope of Work and Delivery Methodology
Phase 1 - Inception, Scoping and Content Adaptation
Review existing MSDS for all levels of care (Cat-I, II, III), PHCC regulations, HIPC e-certification content and learning platform functionality.
Undertake a rapid need assessment to identify sequencing of priority MSDS areas.
Agree with PHCC on: 
module sequencing and phased rollout
indicative learning objectives and structure
certification approach aligned with existing practices
Following agreement on sequencing and module structure, adapt MSDS reference materials into initial structured e-certification modules, building on the HIPC model.
Develop bilingual (English and Urdu) learning content, based on feasibility.
Prepare supporting materials (presentations, job aids, simplified guidance, basic multimedia)
Develop practical assessment tools (e.g., quizzes, short exercises)
Conduct iterative content review and validation with PHCC
Phase 2: Integration and Pilot Testing
Upload and integrate MSDS modules within the existing learning system.
Support course setup, navigation, and learner registration.
Enable basic learner tracking, completion monitoring, and certification issuance.
Address practical usability and accessibility improvements.
Develop simple learning system administration and course management guidance.
Conduct pilot implementation across each healthcare category.
Pilot Design: The pilot will run across 2 districts (duration decided upon inception), selected to represent Punjab’s geographic and sectoral diversity. Proposed selection criteria include;
Mix of urban/rural districts;
Inclusion of at least 2 districts with high density of facilities;
Mix of public and private HCEs;
Existing PHCC regional presence for monitoring.
Target scale : 200–250 healthcare professionals across Cat-I, II, and III, covering all nine modules. Rationale: This sample enables testing usability across user types and settings before full rollout. Learning modality: The pilot will be fully digital via PHCC’s LMS, with optional facility-based group sessions using downloaded content for low-connectivity areas. This blended approach maximises accessibility while testing the scalability of the pure digital model. Pilot findings will directly inform module refinement and LMS setup.
Collect feedback on usability, comprehension, and learner experience.
Where feasible, apply simple pre/post assessments to gauge learning.
Refine modules, assessments, and Learning System setup based on pilot findings
(Note: emphasis on structuring and usability rather than full curriculum re-development or complex competency frameworks)
Phase 3: Institutionalisation and Scale-Up Support
The TA will develop an operational SOP for linking individual physician e-certification to HCE licensing. Proposed mechanism will b;
PHCC will define a minimum % of clinical staff per facility category that must complete relevant MSDS modules for licensing/renewal;
Certification data from the LMS will be integrated into PHCC’s licensing database. This creates facility-level incentives because: 
a) HCEs must demonstrate workforce competency to maintain licensure;
b) It shifts from one-time compliance to continuous professional development;
c) It allows smaller PHC facilities to meet standards without costly in-person training.
Final policy will be determined by PHCC during institutionalisation, with TA providing technical options and global benchmarks.
Develop practical SOPs for: 
Module specific updates
Learning system administration
Certification management
Orient designated PHCC focal persons on course delivery and system use.
Complete handover of: 
Module content and materials
Assessment tools
Provide indicative recommendations for: 
Future module expansion
Strengthening CPD pathways
Recommend linking the e-certification programme results with licensing process.
The e-certification programme will be progressively linked to PHCC licensing and renewal processes. While certification is completed by individual healthcare providers, healthcare establishments may be required to demonstrate availability of certified personnel as part of compliance requirements. This mechanism will incentivise healthcare establishments, particularly primary healthcare facilities, to ensure staff participation in certification programmes, thereby strengthening facility-level compliance with MSDS
Promote the programme across all categories of HCEs including primary healthcare.
Sustainability and Institutionalisation
Designated PHCC focal persons and responsible units will be identified during inception to support content development, review, deployment, and ongoing management
A progressive co-development approach will be adopted, enabling PHCC to gradually take on greater responsibility for content review, course management, and delivery.
Content review processes will be light-touch and feasible, supporting periodic updates.
All learning resources, source files, assessment materials, and guidance documents will be formally handed over to PHCC in editable formats
The TA will provide indicative guidance on future expansion, including options for additional modules and continued use of e-certification to support professional development.
The approach will support a repeatable and adaptable model for future module development, without requiring significant additional system development or external inputs.
The approach supports long-term institutionalisation by embedding certification within regulatory processes, strengthening continuous professional development pathways, and ensuring scalability through existing digital infrastructure..
Deliverables
Inception Package (Slide Deck and Workplan): Scope, sequencing across nine MSDS areas, and overall implementation approach.
MSDS e-Certification Modules – Package 1: Initial set of (4-5) structured modules with content, assessments, and supporting materials.
MSDS e-Certification Modules – Package 2 (Completed Set with Integration): Full set of nine modules finalised, refined through pilot, and configured on digital learning platform.
Final e-Certification Package and Institutionalisation Note.
Position Title:
Research Associate – Digital Learning & Coordination Support (Junior National)
Duty Station: Lahore (with travel as required)
Duration / LOE: Mid-August 2026 – March 2027 (LOE 120 days – subject to change until the start of the TA)
Reporting To: Team Lead – Health Systems & Regulatory Expert
Role Purpose
Provide digital learning, coordination, documentation, and operational support for implementation of the MSDS e-Certification Programme, including learner administration, pilot activities, stakeholder engagement, and reporting.
Key Roles & Responsibilities
Support LMS testing, learner registration, access, and basic administration.
Coordinate stakeholder meetings, workshops, pilot activities, and follow-up actions.
Assist with digital learning support and operational troubleshooting during implementation.
Maintain participant records, trackers, meeting documentation, and action logs.
Support workshop organisation, communications, and logistical arrangements.
Assist with pilot monitoring, reporting, and compilation of learner feedback.
Support preparation of deliverables and institutionalisation documentation.
Undertake other programme support tasks assigned by the Team Lead.
Requirements
Technical Expertise
Bachelor’s degree in Public Health, Management Sciences, Social Sciences, Information Systems, or related discipline.
Minimum 5 years of overall professional experience.
Experience in programme coordination, digital learning support, learner administration, or project implementation preferred.
Experience supporting workshops, stakeholder engagement, and documentation is desirable.
Core Competencies
Stakeholder coordination
LMS and learner support
Workshop management
Logistics management
Communication
Reporting and documentation

job_title: Coordinator Health and Nutrition
job_description:
CHILD SAFEGUARDING:
Level 3: The post holder will have contact with children and/or young people either frequently (e.g. once a week or more) or intensively (e.g. four days in one month or more or overnight) because they work country programs; or are visiting country programs; or because they are responsible for implementing the police checking/vetting process staff.
ROLE PURPOSE:
The Health and Nutrition Coordinator will provide technical and programmatic support to ensure that health, nutrition, food safety, and related child well-being considerations are effectively integrated into the implementation of the Sindh Sustainable School Meals (SSSM) Project, implemented under the USDA McGovern-Dole International Food for Education and Child Nutrition Program, in partnership with the School Education & Literacy Department (SE&LD), Government of Sindh.
The position will support the planning, coordination, implementation, monitoring, and quality assurance of project activities related to school meals, child nutrition, health, hygiene, food safety, and nutrition-sensitive interventions. The role will work closely with the project’s education, school meals, WASH, monitoring, and government coordination teams to ensure that health and nutrition activities are evidence-based, aligned with USDA and Government of Sindh requirements, and responsive to the needs of school-age children.
The Health and Nutrition Coordinator will provide technical guidance on nutrition and health-related components of the project, including nutrition education and awareness, healthy eating practices, food safety and hygiene, school-based health and nutrition messaging, and linkages between school meals, WASH, and child health and well-being. The position will also support the development and review of technical guidelines, training materials, tools, and approaches for project staff, teachers, cooks, school committees, and other relevant stakeholders.
The role will contribute to coordination with SE&LD and other relevant government departments, technical partners, and stakeholders on health and nutrition matters, including participation in relevant technical forums, consultations, and joint planning processes. The position will also support monitoring of health and nutrition indicators, documentation of results and lessons learned, identification of implementation gaps, and development of recommendations to strengthen the quality, effectiveness, and sustainability of the SSSM school meals programme.
The position requires strong technical knowledge of school health and nutrition, excellent coordination and communication skills, and the ability to translate technical nutrition and health concepts into practical interventions within a large-scale school meals programme. The role will require regular engagement with field teams, schools, government counterparts, and communities across the project districts and a strong commitment to improving the health, nutrition, learning, and overall well-being of school-age children.
SCOPE OF ROLE:
Reports to: Education Specialist
Staff Reporting to this role: No
KEY AREAS OF ACCOUNTABILITY :
1. Health and Nutrition Technical Planning and Strategy:
Lead the technical planning and coordination of the Health and Nutrition component of the Sindh Sustainable School Meals (SSSM) Project, ensuring alignment with USDA McGovern-Dole requirements, project objectives, Government of Sindh priorities, and relevant national standards and guidelines.
Develop, review, and periodically update the project’s Health and Nutrition workplan and technical implementation approach, including nutrition education, healthy eating practices, food safety, hygiene, and linkages between school meals, WASH, and child health and well-being.
Provide technical inputs to annual workplans, implementation plans, budgets, and project strategies to ensure that health and nutrition considerations are appropriately integrated across project components.
Monitor emerging health, nutrition, food safety, and school health issues that may affect project implementation and recommend appropriate adaptations to project approaches.
Ensure that the specific health and nutrition needs of school-age children, including vulnerable and underserved children, are reflected in project planning and implementation.
2. Technical Assessment and Programme Design:
Lead or provide technical support to health and nutrition-related assessments in coordination with the MEAL, Education, WASH, School Meals, and other relevant teams.
Analyse assessment findings and translate them into practical recommendations for strengthening school meals, nutrition education, food safety, hygiene, and other health and nutrition interventions.
Provide technical review and guidance on project activities, tools, guidelines, training materials, and approaches related to health and nutrition.
Contribute to the design and development of nutrition-sensitive, nutrition-specific and school-based health interventions that complement the provision of USDA commodities and school meals.
Provide technical inputs to concept notes, proposals, donor submissions, project modifications, and other relevant programme documents, as required.
3. Technical Guidance, Implementation and Quality Assurance:
Provide technical guidance to project teams, field staff, partners, schools, and other relevant stakeholders on the effective implementation of Health and Nutrition activities.
Support the integration of nutrition, food safety, hygiene, and health considerations throughout the school meals programme, from food preparation and handling to consumption at school level.
Provide technical guidance on appropriate nutrition messages, healthy eating practices, dietary diversity, micronutrient considerations, and other relevant nutrition topics within the scope of the project.
Support the development and implementation of appropriate food safety and hygiene standards and procedures for school meal preparation, storage, handling, cooking, and serving.
Work closely with the WASH team to strengthen the linkages between school meals, safe water, sanitation, hygiene practices, and child health.
Conduct regular field visits to project schools and implementation sites to assess the quality of Health and Nutrition activities, identify implementation gaps, and provide corrective technical guidance.
Review progress against Health and Nutrition activities, indicators, targets, and workplans and recommend corrective or acceleration measures where required.
Provide technical inputs to project reports, success stories, case studies, and other donor and management reporting requirements.
4. MEAL, Monitoring and Learning:
Work closely with the MEAL team to develop and implement a Health and Nutrition monitoring framework and plan, aligned with the SSSM results framework and USDA reporting requirements.
Support the development and review of Health and Nutrition indicators, monitoring tools, data collection methodologies, and reporting formats.
Analyze monitoring and assessment data to identify trends, implementation gaps, and opportunities for improving the quality and effectiveness of project interventions.
Ensure that findings from monitoring, assessments, feedback mechanisms, and field observations are translated into practical programme improvements.
Contribute to documentation of lessons learned, good practices, innovations, and evidence related to school meals, nutrition, food safety, and child health.
Support programme teams in using evidence and data to strengthen implementation and demonstrate project results.
5. Capacity Strengthening and Technical Support:
Conduct learning and capacity needs assessments for project staff, partner staff, teachers, cooks, school management committees, and other relevant stakeholders involved in school meals and related activities.
Develop and implement capacity-building plans on relevant Health and Nutrition topics, including nutrition awareness, food safety, hygiene, healthy eating, safe food handling, and school-based nutrition practices.
Develop, review, and facilitate technical training materials, guidance notes, job aids, and other learning resources.
Coach and mentor project and partner staff to strengthen their technical capacity and confidence in implementing Health and Nutrition activities.
Provide technical support to school-level actors to promote sustainable and practical health, nutrition, hygiene, and food safety practices.
6. Government and Stakeholder Coordination:
Support effective coordination with SE&LD, Health Department, Government of Sindh, and other relevant government departments and technical stakeholders on Health and Nutrition aspects of the SSSM Project.
Represent the project in relevant technical meetings, workshops, consultations, and coordination forums related to school health, nutrition, food safety, and school meals, as delegated.
Establish and maintain effective working relationships with relevant government counterparts, technical agencies, partners, and other stakeholders.
Support harmonization of project approaches, tools, and technical messages with relevant government policies, standards, and guidelines.
Facilitate technical discussions with stakeholders to address implementation challenges and identify opportunities for strengthening the health and nutrition component of the project.
7. Accountability, Safeguarding and Quality Standards:
Ensure that Health and Nutrition interventions are implemented in accordance with USDA McGovern-Dole requirements, Save the Children policies and procedures, Government of Sindh standards, and relevant national and international technical guidance.
Promote child safeguarding, protection, inclusion, gender sensitivity, and accountability across Health and Nutrition activities.
Work with the Accountability/MEAL team to ensure that children, caregivers, teachers, and other relevant stakeholders have appropriate opportunities to provide feedback on school meals and related health and nutrition interventions.
Ensure that feedback and complaints relevant to food quality, meal acceptability, hygiene, safety, and nutrition are appropriately documented, analysed, and addressed.
Identify and escalate technical, food safety, health, or nutrition risks that may affect children or the quality of programme delivery.
8. Representation, Advocacy and Organizational Learning:
Represent the SSSM Project in relevant Health, Nutrition, School Health, Food Safety, and School Meals coordination forums, as appropriate.
Promote the importance of school meals as an integrated intervention contributing to child nutrition, health, school attendance, participation, and learning.
Support evidence-based advocacy with government and other stakeholders on strengthening school health and nutrition systems and sustainable school meal approaches.
Document and disseminate lessons learned, promising practices, innovations, and evidence generated through the SSSM Project.
Contribute to project learning events, technical workshops, publications, case studies, and other knowledge-management initiatives.
9. General Responsibilities:
Demonstrate leadership and commitment to Save the Children’s values, policies, Child Safeguarding, Code of Conduct, Health and Safety, Gender Equality, Inclusion, and Accountability principles.
Ensure that all Health and Nutrition activities are implemented in a child-centred, inclusive, culturally appropriate, and participatory manner.
Maintain professional and constructive relationships with project teams, government counterparts, partners, schools, communities, and other stakeholders.
Undertake any other Health and Nutrition-related responsibilities assigned by the supervisor that contribute to the effective implementation and achievement of SSSM Project objectives.

holds self-accountable for making decisions, managing resources efficiently, achieving and role modelling Save the Children values
holds the team and partners accountable to deliver on their responsibilities - giving them the freedom to deliver in the best way they see fit, providing the necessary development to improve performance and applying appropriate consequences when results are not achieved.

future orientated, thinks strategically and on a global scale.

values diversity, sees it as a source of competitive strength
approachable, good listener, easy to talk to.

develops and encourages new and innovative solutions
willing to take disciplined risks.

honest, encourages openness and transparency; demonstrates highest levels of integrity
QUALIFICATIONS:
Essential :
Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Nutrition, Public Health, Food Science, Health Sciences, Nursing, Dietetics, or another relevant health and nutrition-related discipline from a recognized university.
At least 5–7 years of relevant professional experience in health, nutrition, school health, school feeding, community nutrition, food safety, or related programmes, preferably with an NGO, UN agency, government institution, or other development organization.

job_title: PUBLIC HEALTH EXPERT – TEAM LEAD
job_description:
SENIOR NATIONAL STTA - PUBLIC HEALTH EXPERT – TEAM LEAD
E4H KPTA: STRENGTHENING PUBLIC SECTOR INSTITUTIONS FOR MULTISECTORAL SURGE CAPACITY RESPONSE
Programme Overview
Evidence for Health (E4H) is a Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO)-funded programme aimed at strengthening Pakistan's healthcare system, thereby decreasing the burden of illness and saving lives. E4H provides technical assistance (TA) to the Federal, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP), and Punjab governments, and is being implemented by Palladium along with Oxford Policy Management (OPM).
Through its flexible, embedded, and demand-driven model, E4H supports the government to achieve a resilient health system that is prepared for health emergencies, responsive to the latest evidence, and delivers equitable, quality, and efficient healthcare services. Specifically, E4H delivers TA across three outputs:
Output 1: Strengthened integrated health security, with a focus on preparing and responding to health emergencies, including pandemics.
Output 2: Strengthened evidence-based decision-making to drive health sector performance and accountability.
Output 3: Improved implementation of Universal Health Coverage, with a focus on ending preventable deaths.
Background
Pakistan faces recurring public health emergencies that require a skilled multisectoral workforce capable of rapid mobilisation and coordinated response. The 2023 Joint External Evaluation highlighted a critical gap in this area, scoring Pakistan 1 out of 5 for workforce surge capacity during a public health event.
In response, a national multisectoral surge capacity training package has been developed to strengthen workforce readiness through core and role-specific competencies, practical training approaches and simulation-based learning.
However, translating this national package into sustainable provincial workforce capacity requires contextualisation to provincial health systems and emergency response arrangements, alongside stronger institutional capacity to deliver and sustain the training.
Public sector education and training institutions, including medical universities, health services academies and other relevant institutions, provide established platforms for embedding surge capacity competencies within postgraduate and continuing professional education. Targeted technical assistance is therefore required to strengthen faculty capacity and institutionalise the contextualised training within these existing platforms.
Problem Statement
Provincial public sector education and training institutions currently lack the institutional capacity and mechanisms to contextualise, deliver and sustainably embed multisectoral surge capacity training within existing postgraduate and continuing professional development programmes. As a result, surge capacity training remains largely dependent on stand-alone initiatives, limiting its scale, continuity and alignment with provincial emergency preparedness and response requirements.
Despite the growing emphasis on health security and emergency preparedness, surge capacity training is not yet systematically embedded within provincial academic and continuing professional development pathways. Training opportunities may remain dependent on stand-alone or externally supported activities, limiting continuity, scale and institutional ownership.
Goal and Objective(s)
The overall goal of this technical assistance is to establish sustainable institutional capacity within provincial public sector education and training institutions to deliver multisectoral surge capacity training aligned with KP’s emergency preparedness and response needs. We will achieve this by pursuing three objectives:
Objectives
Objective 1: Contextualise the national multisectoral surge capacity training package to Khyber pakhtunkhwa’s (KP’s) health system, workforce and emergency preparedness and response context.
Objective 2: Strengthen institutional and faculty capacity to design, deliver and sustain competency-based, multisectoral surge capacity training.
Objective 3: Institutionalise surge capacity training within relevant postgraduate or continuing professional development pathways, with appropriate mechanisms for quality assurance and continuous improvement.
Scope of Work and Methodology
The technical assistance will support provincial public sector education and training institutions to contextualise the national multisectoral surge capacity training package, strengthen faculty and government capacity to deliver it, and embed surge capacity competencies within relevant postgraduate and continuing professional development (CPD) pathways. The approach will build on the existing national package rather than develop new content in parallel, combining provincial contextualisation, joint academic–government capacity strengthening and institutionalisation. The TA will be delivered through four interlinked phases:
Phase 1: Inception, institutional assessment and stakeholder engagement
The technical assistance will begin with a rapid review of the national surge capacity package and existing institutional arrangements for postgraduate education, CPD and curriculum approval. Consultations with academic institutions, the Department of Health (DOH), Provincial Health Services Academy (PHSA) and relevant multisectoral stakeholders will identify priority workforce competencies, institutional requirements and appropriate entry points for integration. This phase will also establish arrangements for government and development partner engagement, including coordination with relevant Pandemic Fund, WHO and UKHSA-supported initiatives.
Phase 2: Provincial contextualisation and validation
Working jointly with faculty and government stakeholders, the technical assistance will contextualise the national package to KP’s health system, emergency risks, workforce roles and preparedness and response arrangements, while retaining its core competency framework and technical integrity. This will include adapting case studies, scenarios, practical and simulation-based exercises and learning materials to reflect provincial realities and relevant One Health and multisectoral dimensions wherever applicable. The contextualised package will be reviewed and validated with relevant academic, government and technical stakeholders.
Phase 3: Faculty and institutional capacity strengthening
The technical assistance will use a training-of-trainers and learning-by-doing approach to strengthen a core group of faculty and relevant government counterparts in competency-based teaching, facilitation, simulation and tabletop exercises, assessment and practical application of surge capacity competencies. Faculty will progressively co-facilitate sessions and receive structured coaching and feedback, building the capacity to independently deliver and periodically update the training. Joint participation of academic and government stakeholders will also strengthen the connection between classroom learning and provincial emergency preparedness, coordination and deployment functions.
Phase 4: Institutionalisation within postgraduate and CPD systems
The technical assistance will support participating institutions to map surge capacity competencies against relevant postgraduate public health curricula and CPD pathways and determine appropriate options for integration, delivery and assessment. This will include supporting relevant academic and institutional review and approval processes and establishing practical arrangements for continued delivery, quality assurance and periodic updating. The emphasis will be on using existing education and training systems to create a sustainable provincial mechanism rather than a parallel or externally dependent training programme.
Sustainability: Capacity Building, Institutionalisation, and/or Transition Planning
Capacity building: As described in Phase 3 of the methodology, the technical assistance will establish a core pool of faculty and relevant government counterparts able to deliver competency-based, practical and simulation-oriented surge capacity training. A training-of-trainers and learning-by-doing approach, including co-facilitation, coaching and structured feedback, will strengthen their ability to deliver, assess and periodically update the training independently.
Institutionalisation: As described in Phase 4, surge capacity competencies will be mapped to relevant postgraduate and CPD pathways and incorporated through existing curriculum, academic and institutional approval processes. Delivery, assessment and quality assurance arrangements will be embedded within established education and training systems, with government and institutional stakeholders involved in validation and oversight.
Transition and sustainability: Responsibility for routine delivery, faculty development, curriculum review and updating will transition to participating public sector education and training institutions and relevant provincial stakeholders following completion of the TA. The contextualised package, trained faculty and agreed quality assurance arrangements will provide the basis for continued delivery without reliance on E4H-supported implementation.
Scale-up: The institutional model will provide a pathway for adapting the training for additional CPD programmes and relevant health workforce cadres, in line with provincial and national surge capacity priorities and available institutional resources.
Timeline and Days
The proposed LOE is 40 days from October 2026 to December 2026, subject to final confirmation from client.
Requirement
Technical Expertise
Ph.D. in Public Health after MBBS/BDS/medical degree is mandatory.
Minimum 15 years of relevant experience in public health, including emergency preparedness and response, surveillance, health systems, risk assessment, and evidence-informed decision-making.
Must have worked for at least 2 years during the last 5 years in a public-sector postgraduate (PG) institution, preferably in KP.
Demonstrated experience in multisectoral coordination, public health workforce development, training, and use of data for decision-making.
Strong analytical, planning, communication, coordination, and professional judgement skills.
Competencies
Strong critical thinking and professional judgement, with the ability to analyse and interpret public health information, solve problems and support evidence-informed decisions; effective multidisciplinary teamwork, coordination and relationship-building skills; clear communication and ability to explain complex concepts; strong planning, organisation, adaptability and attention to detail.

The emphasis will be on using existing education and training systems to create a sustainable provincial mechanism rather than a parallel or externally dependent training programme.
Sustainability: Capacity Building, Institutionalisation, and/or Transition Planning
Capacity building: As described in Phase 3 of the methodology, the technical assistance will establish a core pool of faculty and relevant government counterparts able to deliver competency-based, practical and simulation-oriented surge capacity training. A training-of-trainers and learning-by-doing approach, including co-facilitation, coaching and structured feedback, will strengthen their ability to deliver, assess and periodically update the training independently.
Institutionalisation: As described in Phase 4, surge capacity competencies will be mapped to relevant postgraduate and CPD pathways and incorporated through existing curriculum, academic and institutional approval processes. Delivery, assessment and quality assurance arrangements will be embedded within established education and training systems, with government and institutional stakeholders involved in validation and oversight.
Transition and sustainability: Responsibility for routine delivery, faculty development, curriculum review and updating will transition to participating public sector education and training institutions and relevant provincial stakeholders following completion of the TA. The contextualised package, trained faculty and agreed quality assurance arrangements will provide the basis for continued delivery without reliance on E4H-supported implementation.
Scale-up: The institutional model will provide a pathway for adapting the training for additional CPD programmes and relevant health workforce cadres, in line with provincial and national surge capacity priorities and available institutional resources.

The proposed LOE is 40 days from October 2026 to December 2026, subject to final confirmation from client.

job_title: Consultancy Services for Flood Hazard, Soil Runoff and Erosion Assessment, Protective Asset Siting and Community Awareness District Lasbela
job_description:
TERMS OF REFERENCE (TORs)
Consultancy Services for Flood Hazard, Soil Runoff and Erosion Assessment, Protective Asset Siting and Community Awareness District Lasbela
1. Background
A National level non-governmental organization (NGO) intends to engage a qualified and experienced consultancy firm/consultant to undertake a comprehensive Flood Hazard and Soil Runoff Study covering a single contiguous study area comprising four target villages located along the corridor affected by the 2022 floods.
The assignment is intended to generate reliable technical evidence on flood hazards, inundation patterns, soil runoff and erosion, exposure of communities and assets, and suitable locations for protective and water-related infrastructure.
The study will combine survey-grade elevation data, high-resolution satellite imagery, field observations and validation against the observed 2022 flood event. The results will support evidence-based planning, disaster risk reduction, climate resilience and appropriate siting of protective assets.
In addition to technical analysis and mapping, the consultancy will develop two animated awareness videos in simple local language to communicate key flood and soil runoff risks and recommended actions to communities.
2. Purpose of the Consultancy
The purpose of this consultancy is to conduct an integrated flood hazard and soil runoff/erosion assessment of the defined study area and provide technically sound recommendations for reducing flood and erosion risks to communities, homes, agricultural land and other critical assets.
The assignment will establish:
Areas likely to be inundated under defined rainfall/flood conditions.
The extent and depth of potential flooding.
Homes, infrastructure, agricultural land and other assets exposed to flood hazards.
Areas experiencing concentrated surface runoff.
Locations vulnerable to soil erosion and soil loss.
Priority areas requiring protective measures.
Appropriate locations for protective and water-management assets.
Practical information that can be communicated to communities in an accessible manner.
3. Objectives of the Assignment
The specific objectives are to:
Conduct a detailed flood hazard assessment for the four target villages and the surrounding flood corridor.
Develop reliable flood inundation and hazard maps using appropriate hydrological, hydraulic, GIS and remote-sensing techniques.
Assess the exposure of houses, population, infrastructure, agricultural land and other relevant assets to flood hazards.
Assess surface runoff patterns, soil loss and erosion-prone areas.
Identify areas where runoff and erosion are concentrated and determine their potential impacts.
Validate the technical findings through field observations and comparison with the observed 2022 flood event.
Identify priority locations for flood protection, drainage, water management and erosion-control interventions.
Provide technically justified recommendations for the siting of protective and water-related assets.
Prepare an accessible community-level communication package, including two animated awareness videos in simple local language.
Provide with a complete technical report, maps, spatial datasets and other relevant study outputs.
4. Scope of Work
The selected consultant/consultancy firm shall undertake, at minimum, the following activities.
i. Inception and Study Planning
The consultant shall:
Review all available project documents, existing studies, maps and relevant secondary information
Review information relating to the 2022 flood event
Define and confirm the study boundary covering the four target villages and their flood corridor
Develop a detailed methodology and work plan
Identify required datasets, surveys and field investigations
Agree on the proposed methodology with organization before commencement of detailed analysis
An Inception Report shall be submitted for review and approval.
ii. Topographic and Elevation Assessment
The consultant shall utilize appropriate survey-grade elevation information for the study area.
Activities may include:
Review and processing of available topographic/elevation data
Ground verification where required
Identification of drainage paths, low-lying areas, natural channels and flow accumulation zones
Preparation of an appropriate Digital Elevation Model
Identification of critical elevation points affecting flood movement and runoff.
The consultant shall ensure that the elevation data used are of sufficient accuracy for the intended flood and runoff analysis.
iii. Satellite and Remote-Sensing Analysis
The consultant shall acquire and analyse suitable high-resolution satellite imagery and other relevant remote-sensing datasets covering the wider study area.
The analysis shall, where appropriate, identify:
Land use and land cover
Existing drainage channels and flow paths
Agricultural areas
Areas affected by erosion
Changes associated with flood events
iv. Flood Hazard and Inundation Assessment
The consultant shall conduct a flood hazard assessment using appropriate hydrological and/or hydraulic modelling techniques.
The assessment shall, as applicable, include:
Analysis of relevant rainfall and hydrological information
Identification of flood sources and flow paths
Assessment of flood-prone areas
Flood inundation modelling under defined rainfall/flood conditions
Estimation of flood extent
Estimation of flood depth and/or other relevant flood hazard parameters
Identification of high-, medium- and low-risk areas, where appropriate
Preparation of village-level and study-area flood hazard maps
The consultant shall clearly document the assumptions, datasets, modelling approach and limitations.
v. 2022 Flood Event Validation
The consultant shall validate the assessment against the observed 2022 flood event.
Validation may include:
Review of historical satellite imagery
Review of available flood records
Field verification
Community consultations and collection of local knowledge
Comparison of modelled and observed flood extents
Identification of discrepancies and refinement of the model where necessary.
The consultant shall clearly explain the validation methodology and results in the final report.
5. Flood Exposure Assessment
The consultant shall conduct a quantitative exposure assessment for the identified flood hazard areas.
The assessment should, where data are available, cover:
Residential houses
Population/households
Roads and access routes
Schools and health facilities
Water supply infrastructure
Agricultural land
Livestock-related assets
Public/community infrastructure
The consultant shall quantify the number and/or area of exposed assets and present the findings in an understandable format.
6. Soil Runoff and Erosion Assessment
The consultant shall undertake a detailed assessment of surface runoff, soil loss and erosion risk within the study area.
The assessment shall include, as appropriate:
Identification of major runoff generation areas
Mapping of surface drainage and runoff concentration
Identification of erosion-prone locations
Assessment of soil characteristics relevant to runoff and erosion
Assessment of land use/land cover impacts
Estimation and/or modelling of soil loss
Identification of areas requiring erosion-control measures
Preparation of soil runoff and erosion-risk maps
The consultant shall clearly describe the methodology, assumptions and datasets used for estimating soil loss and runoff.
7. Protective and Water Asset Siting Recommendations
Based on the flood, runoff and erosion assessments, the consultant shall identify and recommend suitable locations for protective and water-related assets.
Potential interventions may include, but are not limited to:
Flood protection structures
Drainage improvements
Water diversion structures
Retention/detention measures
Erosion-control structures
Embankments or protective barriers
For each priority location, the consultant shall provide:
Location/coordinates
Identified hazard or problem
Technical justification
Priority level
Recommended type of intervention
Preliminary considerations for implementation
The recommendations shall be based on the findings of the study and shall not be common.
8. Community Consultation and Field Validation
The consultant shall conduct appropriate field visits and consultations with relevant stakeholders and communities in the four target villages.
The purpose shall be to:
Verify flood pathways and affected areas
Document community observations regarding the 2022 flood
Identify locations of recurring flooding and erosion
Verify important community assets
Collect relevant local knowledge
Validate technical findings
Support development of appropriate community awareness messages.
The consultant shall ensure that consultations are conducted in an inclusive and culturally appropriate manner.
9. Community Awareness Videos
The consultant shall develop two animated awareness videos based on the technical findings of the study.
The videos shall:
Be designed for community-level understanding
Use simple and clear local language
Explain key flood and/or runoff risks
Communicate practical preparedness and risk-reduction measures
Incorporate appropriate visual animation
Be understandable to audiences with limited technical knowledge
The consultant shall coordinate with service seeker organization regarding the language, script, key messages and final content before production.
Final videos shall be provided in commonly usable digital formats.
10. Key Deliverables

The final report shall, at minimum, contain:

12. GIS Maps and Data Package
The consultant shall provide all relevant spatial outputs in editable GIS formats.
The final data package should include, as applicable:
Flood hazard maps

Runoff maps

Recommended intervention locations
Digital Elevation Model and relevant derivatives

All GIS data shall be provided in commonly usable/editable formats and with appropriate metadata
13. Duration of Assignment
The total duration of the consultancy shall be sixteen (16) weeks from the date of contract signing.
The consultant shall submit a detailed work plan showing the proposed schedule for fieldwork, data processing, modelling, analysis, consultation, reporting and production of awareness materials.
14. Required Qualifications and Experience
The assignment shall be undertaken by a qualified consultancy firm or suitably qualified multidisciplinary team with demonstrated experience in flood risk assessment, hydrological/hydraulic modelling, GIS and soil erosion/runoff assessment.
The firm/team should have:
Relevant academic qualifications in hydrology, hydraulic engineering, water resources engineering, civil engineering, environmental sciences, geospatial sciences, geography, soil science or related disciplines;
Demonstrated experience in flood hazard and inundation assessment;
Experience in GIS and remote sensing
Experience in hydrological/hydraulic modelling
Experience in soil erosion and runoff assessment
Experience in field surveys and ground validation
Experience in developing technical maps and spatial databases
Experience in climate/disaster risk reduction or resilience-related assignments is desirable

15. Indicative Key Personnel

job_title: Consultancy Study on Climate Change-Induced Loss and Damage in Keti Bandar Tehsil, District Thatta, Sindh
job_description:
Terms of Reference (ToR)
Consultancy
Study on Climate Change-Induced Loss and Damage
in Keti Bandar Tehsil, District Thatta, Sindh
1. Background
German Red Cross supports Pakistan Red Crescent Society (PRCS) in undertaking a tehsil-level Climate Change-Induced Loss and Damage (L&D) Study in Keti Bandar, District Thatta, Sindh, under the Climate Advocacy and Coordination for Resilient Action (CACRA) project, financially assisted by the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ). The study will apply an explicit climate-change lens and use a project-developed assessment framework informed by the UNFCCC Loss and Damage architecture, including relevant work of the Warsaw International Mechanism for Loss and Damage (WIM), together with other recognized climate-risk assessment approaches where appropriate. It aims to generate evidence on economic and non-economic loss and damage associated with the adverse effects of climate change and climate-related hazards, including both extreme events and slow-onset processes, to support climate-resilient programming, adaptation planning, policy engagement and advocacy.
The consultant must use the project-developed Research Framework for the Loss and Damage Study in Pakistan as the technical basis, adapting it to the tehsil context and recommending only those refinements required for methodological rigor, feasibility and local relevance. Particular attention in Keti Bandar shall be given to relevant coastal and hydro-meteorological hazards and slow-onset processes, including cyclone/storm surge, coastal inundation, sea intrusion/salinity, water stress, extreme heat and other locally evidenced climate-related risks.
2. Objective
To undertake a comprehensive tehsil-level Study on Climate Change-Induced Loss and Damage in Keti Bandar, applying an explicit climate-change lens to assess the nature, scale, distribution and evolution of economic and non-economic Loss and Damage associated with climate variability, changing climate-related hazards and slow-onset processes, and to examine how exposure, vulnerability, adaptation and residual climate impacts shape Loss and Damage, in accordance with the project’s UNFCCC/WIM-informed assessment framework.
3. Scope of Work
The following A and B sub-sections explain the scope of the assignment.
A. Climate Risk Context
Assess historical climate and hazard trends over a minimum of 15 years and preferably up to 20 years, subject to data availability.
Examine relevant sudden- and slow-onset climate-related hazards and processes, including coastal flooding, cyclones/storm surges, sea intrusion and salinity, water stress, extreme heat, changing rainfall patterns and other locally relevant climate risks.
Assess how climate hazards interact with exposure, vulnerability and adaptive capacity, particularly across climate-sensitive livelihoods and vulnerable population groups.
B. Climate-related Loss & Damage
Assess economic and non-economic Loss and Damage to households, livelihoods, productive assets, basic services, ecosystems and communities.
Examine recurrent, cumulative and potentially irreversible losses, including residual Loss and Damage where coping and adaptation measures are insufficient.
Assess impacts on key climate-sensitive livelihoods and natural resources, particularly fisheries, agriculture, livestock, freshwater, land and coastal ecosystems, including implications for displacement, migration and livelihood changes. Given the high out-migration from Keti Bandar, the methodology must include mechanisms to track and sample displaced households in host areas (e.g., nearby towns or cities) to capture abandoned assets and the full scale of displacement
Assess relevant coping, adaptation, preparedness, early warning and recovery/support mechanisms, and identify key gaps contributing to or influencing Loss and Damage.
Identify community and institutional priorities for averting, minimizing and addressing Loss and Damage.
4. Expected Deliverables
The consultancy has three main deliverables; a) Inception Report, b) Final agreed L&D Assessment Report, c) PPT of key findings for broader presentation.
4.1. Inception Report
The inception report may include; Keti Bandar-specific operationalization of the approved Research Framework; proposed and justified household/qualitative sample; hazard–livelihood stratification; field-team composition and deployment plan; 15–20-year climate/hazard secondary-data analysis plan (including the GIS/remote sensing methodology for land-loss mapping); proposed secondary data sources; data-quality/triangulation approach; ethical and safeguarding measures; and any technically necessary refinements to the existing tools.
4.2. Loss and Damage Assessment Report
The report would have following indicative outlines. As these outlines are indicative and may be refined at the inception stage in consultation with the project team, while ensuring that all key assessment dimensions specified in the Scope of Work are adequately addressed.
Executive Summary: Key findings on climate-induced Loss & Damage, Major affected groups, livelihoods and areas, Key conclusions and priority recommendations.
Introduction and Methodology: Assessment purpose, scope and Keti Bandar context, Research framework, methodology and data sources, Coverage, limitations and uncertainties.
Climate Risk Context: Historical climate and hazard trends, covering a minimum of 15 years and preferably up to 20 years, subject to data availability, Relevant sudden- and slow-onset climate-related hazards, Exposure, vulnerability and adaptive capacity, Key climate-risk patterns.
Economic Loss & Damage: Losses to livelihoods, income and productive assets, Housing, infrastructure and basic services, Fisheries, agriculture, livestock and other climate-sensitive sectors, Direct, indirect, recurrent and cumulative losses, as relevant and measurable.
Non-Economic Loss & Damage: Individuals (including life, health, well-being, mobility/displacement and other relevant individual-level losses), Society (including territory, cultural heritage, indigenous/local knowledge, social and cultural identity, traditional ecological knowledge, place-based cultural identity, loss of sense of place and ancestral connections to land/sea, and other relevant societal losses), Environment ( including biodiversity, ecosystems and ecosystem services and other relevant environmental losses).
Coping, Adaptation and Residual Loss & Damage: Existing coping and adaptation practices, and Residual and potentially irreversible Loss & Damage.
Conclusions and Recommendations
Annexes (Must include relevant GIS maps showing historical land-use/shoreline change and hazard exposure).
4.3. Presentation of key findings: It must be framed in a way to present external public and humanitarian stakeholders.
5. Duration
The consultancy is expected to be completed within approximately two months from the signing of the contract. Bidders may propose a technically justified adjustment to the workplan if required by the final sample size, geographic dispersion or field-access conditions in Keti Bandar.
6. Key responsibilities
The PRCS and GRC will be responsible for:
Develop liaison with Provincial Head Quarter Sindh.
Providing necessary project documents including Loss and Damage assessment framework.
Facilitating for field-level coordination and introductions to relevant local stakeholders (internal & external), authorities and communities, where needed and feasible.
Providing timely feedback on the consultant’s documents or consultancy deliverables.
Releasing the consultancy fee as per signed agreement.
The consultant will be responsible for:

Identifying, assessing and documenting the quality and limitations of secondary data used.
Coordination with relevant stakeholders in consultation with PRCS and GRC.
Acquiring primary and secondary data, analysing and reporting.
Bearing all expenses associated with this consultancy such as; travel, human resources, logistics, accommodation etc.
7. Required Qualifications, experience, and knowledge
The consultant should have:
An advanced university degree in Climate Change, Environmental Sciences, Environmental Informatics, Disaster Risk Management, Development Studies, Geography, or degree in related discipline.
At least 7 years of professional experience in climate change, disaster risk reduction, vulnerability assessments, or Loss and Damage assessments.
Demonstrated experience designing and leading climate-related mixed-method field assessments, including recruitment/training and management of survey teams, sampling implementation, field quality assurance, KIIs and FGDs.
Strong understanding of the UNFCCC/WIM Loss and Damage agenda and climate-change adaptation architecture, including economic and non-economic loss and damage, comprehensive climate-risk management, extreme events, slow-onset processes, limits to adaptation and residual Loss and Damage.
Demonstrated ability to integrate historical/secondary datasets with household and qualitative evidence; experience with GIS/spatial analysis or remote-sensing data will be an advantage.
Experience working with humanitarian or development organizations, preferably within the Red Cross Red Crescent Movement or similar organizations, will be an asset.
Prior experience in coastal, deltaic or slow-onset climate-risk contexts, particularly in Sindh or comparable settings, will be an asset.
8. Reporting
