job_title: Technical Director Immunization
job_description:
Overview:
Jhpiego is an international non-profit health organization affiliated with The Johns Hopkins University. For more than 50 years and in over 150 countries, Jhpiego has worked to improve the health of women, children, and families by strengthening health systems and delivering high-quality, evidence-based interventions.
Jhpiego seeks a highly experienced Technical Director, Immunization to provide strategic and technical leadership for its immunization portfolio in Pakistan. The Technical Director will serve as Jhpiego's senior technical authority on immunization and vaccine-preventable disease prevention and control, providing expert guidance to government counterparts, Jhpiego programs, donors and partners.
The Technical Director will provide strategic and technical leadership across routine immunization, polio eradication and transition, supplementary immunization activities and campaigns, zero-dose and under-immunized populations, new vaccine introductions, immunization systems strengthening, vaccine-preventable disease surveillance, and outbreak preparedness and vaccination response. The role will ensure that Jhpiego's programs apply current epidemiological evidence, national and global guidance, high-quality immunization implementation, and health system strengthening approaches to drive sustainable improvements in immunization coverage, equity, quality, and health system resilience.
Responsibilities:
1. Strategic and Technical Leadership
Provide overall strategic and technical leadership for Jhpiego’s immunization portfolio in Pakistan and serve as the organization’s senior technical authority on immunization and vaccine-preventable disease prevention and control.
Set technical direction and ensure quality across routine immunization, zero-dose and under-immunized populations, new vaccine introductions, vaccination campaigns/SIAs, VPD surveillance, and outbreak preparedness and response.
Translate national priorities, global guidance, emerging evidence, and epidemiological trends into practical strategies and technical approaches for Jhpiego-supported programs.
Provide senior technical review and guidance to Jhpiego leadership and project teams on immunization strategies, technical approaches, workplans, guidelines, and major deliverables.
Identify emerging immunization priorities, technical gaps, and opportunities for Jhpiego to strengthen its contribution in Pakistan.
2. Immunization Systems, New Vaccines and Service Delivery
Provide senior technical guidance on strengthening routine immunization systems, including service delivery, microplanning, workforce performance, supportive supervision, vaccine management, cold chain, last-mile delivery, and use of immunization data.
Guide strategies to reach zero-dose, under-immunized, and underserved populations and improve coverage, equity, continuity, and quality of immunization services.
Provide technical leadership for new vaccine introductions and optimization, including policy and technical decision-making, readiness assessment, delivery strategies, training, monitoring, and post-introduction learning.
Provide technical oversight for vaccination campaigns and SIAs, including planning, readiness, implementation quality, monitoring, and linkages with routine immunization.
Promote approaches that ensure polio and campaign investments strengthen routine immunization systems, workforce capacity, community engagement, surveillance, and data use.
3. VPD Surveillance, Outbreak Preparedness
Provide senior technical leadership to strengthen linkages between routine immunization, vaccine-preventable disease surveillance, polio eradication, and outbreak preparedness and response.
Support analysis and interpretation of surveillance, epidemiological, immunization, and campaign data to identify immunity gaps, high-risk populations, geographic hotspots, and emerging threats.
Provide technical guidance during suspected or confirmed VPD outbreaks, including risk assessment, identification of affected and at-risk populations, and development of appropriate vaccination response strategies.
Provide technical oversight for outbreak-response vaccination, including target-setting, microplanning, readiness assessment, vaccine and supply requirements, monitoring, corrective action, and post-response review.
Strengthen national and provincial capacity for outbreak preparedness and rapid response, working with EPI, surveillance, PEI, emergency response, and health security structures as appropriate.
Support strategies to maintain essential immunization services during outbreaks, humanitarian emergencies, and other disruptions.
4. Government, Partners, Donors and External Technical Engagement
Serve as a trusted senior technical advisor to the Federal Directorate of Immunization, Provincial EPI programs, Ministry of National Health Services, and other relevant government counterparts.
Represent Jhpiego in national and provincial immunization technical working groups, advisory mechanisms, coordination platforms, and partner forums.
Build and maintain strategic technical relationships with Donors (Gavi, Gates Foundation), WHO, UNICEF, professional associations, academic institutions, civil society, and other immunization partners.
Support national and provincial policy, planning, prioritization, and technical decision-making related to immunization and VPD control.
Position Jhpiego as a recognized technical partner in immunization, vaccine delivery, VPD control, and immunization systems strengthening in Pakistan.
5. Program Quality, Evidence, Learning and Capacity Strengthening
Provide technical oversight to project teams to ensure high-quality implementation and achievement of immunization results.
Review program performance, identify technical and implementation bottlenecks, and guide corrective action and adaptive management.
Promote integrated use of immunization coverage, surveillance, campaign, and program performance data for technical decision-making and continuous improvement.
Guide analysis and interpretation of program results and ensure findings are translated into actionable recommendations for government and project teams.
Mentor and build the technical capacity of Jhpiego staff, government counterparts, and implementing partners through coaching, technical assistance, and supportive supervision.
Support documentation and dissemination of implementation experience, innovations, lessons learned, and effective practices.
6. Portfolio Development and Resource Mobilization
Lead Jhpiego’s technical engagement related to donor supported initiatives (Gavi, Gates Foundation, Department of State, CDC) and emerging investment opportunities in Pakistan.
Support government and partners with immunization strategy development, investment prioritization, and relevant funding applications.
Identify opportunities to expand Jhpiego’s immunization portfolio in areas aligned with government priorities and organizational technical strengths.
Provide technical leadership for concept notes, proposals, and donor engagement related to immunization, vaccine delivery, and VPD prevention and control.
Required Qualifications and Skills:
Advanced degree in Medicine, Public Health, Epidemiology, Health Policy, Health Systems, Global Health, or a related field, with specialization in immunization, infectious diseases, health systems strengthening, or public health preferred.
Minimum 10 years of progressively responsible experience in immunization, public health, or health systems strengthening programs.
Demonstrated experience supporting national and subnational immunization programs in Pakistan, including collaboration with Federal Directorate of Immunization (FDI) and provincial Expanded Programme on Immunization (EPI) teams, Polio Eradication Initiative (PEI) and Emergency Operations Center (EOC) structures, National Immunization Technical Advisory Group (NITAG) and other technical advisory mechanisms, as well as national and provincial outbreak preparedness, coordination, and response efforts.
Strong knowledge of routine immunization, polio eradication, vaccine introduction, vaccine-preventable diseases and surveillance, immunization financing, vaccine delivery systems, and health systems strengthening
Experience working with Gavi-funded programs and understanding of Gavi funding mechanisms and country planning processes strongly preferred.
Proven experience engaging ministries of health, donors, UN agencies, and development partners.
Demonstrated success in technical leadership, program management, and stakeholder coordination.
Experience supporting proposal development, resource mobilization, and strategic planning activities.
Excellent analytical, problem-solving, and organizational skills.
Exceptional written and verbal communication skills in English; knowledge of Urdu or other local languages is an asset.
Ability to travel domestically and internationally up to 40% of the time.
Preferred Qualifications:
Experience supporting HPV vaccine introduction, polio eradication/transition, supplemental immunization activities, or other new vaccine introductions.
Experience in outbreak response, emergency vaccination campaigns, polio campaigns, or immunization programming in fragile and hard-to-reach settings.
Experience leading multidisciplinary teams and mentoring technical staff.
Established professional relationships within Pakistan's immunization and public health sector.
Track record of successfully managing donor-funded programs and multi-stakeholder partnerships.
Competencies:
Strategic leadership and vision
Technical excellence in immunization and public health
Stakeholder engagement and diplomacy
Partnership development
Results orientation
Team leadership and mentoring
Resource mobilization and business development
Communication and influencing skills
Data-driven decision making
Cultural sensitivity and adaptability

RFQ for Hiring of a Consultant, Procurement Reference No. PMU/WA/2026/08/23
Part 1: Terms of Reference (TORs)
IHHN through this document requires “Hiring of a Consultant for Mapping and review relevant provincial policies, practices, processes and curricula, while assessing healthcare staff capacity and training needs for delivering sustainable, climate-resilient, gender-responsive and inclusive RMNCH-WASH services at selected PHC sites.
Background and Context
Indus Hospital & Health Network (IHHN), in partnership with WaterAid Pakistan, is implementing the Strengthening Wholistic and Inclusive Systems for Health (SWISH) project through Integration, Prevention, and Women's Empowerment. The project is focusing 10 selected Primary Healthcare Facilities in District Lodhran, Punjab. The project also seeks to institutionalize climate-resilient, inclusive, and sustainable WASH services alongside improved Reproductive, Maternal, Newborn, and Child Health (RMNCH) services, ultimately driving better quality of care, infection prevention and control (IPC), and health outcomes across Punjab.
While, field-level interventions and facility infrastructure improvements are critical in the selected primary healthcare facilities, the long-term sustainability and scale of integrated health and WASH services rely heavily on enabling provincial policies, strategic frameworks, and institutionalized practices.
In this context, the SWISH project design includes a set of activities aimed at assessing and strengthening the policy environment, institutional practices and capacity for integrating WASH within primary MNCH programmes, with particular attention to gender responsiveness, inclusion and climate resilience. The key activities planned to achieve these objectives are outlined below:
Mapping and review of existing relevant Provincial practices, processes, curriculum, policies (National IPC guidelines/framework, provincial health strategy, ADP, PHCC etc.) to deliver and sustain integrated, gender responsive RMNCH and WASH programs.
Conduct Training Need Assessment of Climate Resilient, gender responsive, Inclusive WASH awareness and knowledge amongst healthcare staff cadres (selected PHC sites)
The purpose is to generate actionable, government-owned recommendations that can inform ADP and PC-I formulation, facility-level improvement planning, costing, supervision and convergence between health and WASH investments. The assignment therefore goes beyond a generic review or data-gathering exercise. It will provide a context-specific and practical assessment of policy, institutional and capacity gaps, identify opportunities for better integration of WASH within primary MNCH programming, and assess the readiness and training needs of healthcare staff. The findings will provide actionable recommendations and clear pathways for strengthening the integration of WASH, RMNCH, IPC, gender responsiveness and climate resilience within Punjab's health policies, strategies, planning frameworks and institutional practices.
Purpose of the Consultancy
The purpose of this consultancy is to engage a qualified consultant to undertake a comprehensive mapping, desk review and qualitative assessment of existing policies, budgets, protocols, institutional frameworks and curricula relevant to the delivery of WASH services and practices within primary MNCH programmes. The consultancy will also assess the knowledge, awareness and capacity of relevant healthcare staff through a Training Needs Assessment (TNA), with a particular focus on climate-resilient, gender-responsive and inclusive WASH, RMNCH, Menstrual Hygiene Management (MHM) and Infection Prevention and Control (IPC).
The consultant should demonstrate practical expertise in IPC, RMNCH, WASH in HCFs, PHC systems, Punjab public-sector planning processes, stakeholder facilitation, GEDSI, disability inclusion, climate resilience and high-quality policy writing.
The consultant will work under the technical supervision of the IHHN project team, in accordance with the technical guidance of WaterAid Pakistan, and in coordination with relevant provincial health authorities and other key stakeholders. Consultations/coordination should include P&SHD, DGHS, IRMNCH and Nutrition Program, Punjab Health Care Commission, P&D Board, PHED, DHA, facility managers, frontline providers and community perspectives.
The component wise specific objectives of the consultancy are:
Mapping and review of existing relevant Provincial practices, processes, curriculum, policies (National IPC guidelines/framework, provincial health strategy, ADP, PHCC etc.) to deliver and sustain integrated, gender responsive RMNCH and WASH programs.
Mapping (Identify and compile existing policy documents, processes, practices and curriculum) relevant to RMNCH, WASH, MHM and IPC.
Conduct desk review and key informant interviews with provincial stakeholders (P&SHC, DG Health Office, DG M&E, P&D, PHED, RMNCH).
Analyse alignment with integrated, gender-responsive health services (alignment with climate resilient models).
Prepare and submit a comprehensive review report with recommendations.
Follow up on recommendations to ensure that these are well integrated into planning and policy documents.
Conduct Training Need Assessment of Climate Resilient, gender responsive, Inclusive WASH awareness and knowledge amongst healthcare staff cadres (selected PHC sites).
Develop TNA methodology and its tool.
Coordinate and conduct assessments at selected PHC facilities.
Analyze data to identify gaps in staff knowledge and skills.
Develop TNA report and share with relevant stakeholders (WAP, DoH).
Provide support and monitoring of WASH FIT and WASH IPC practices in MNCH services delivery with HCF-Staff.
[
Expected Outcomes
The activity will contribute to the following outcomes of the SWISH project:
Intermediate Outcome
Increased use of WASH-enhanced MNCH services by women, men and children within targeted primary health care (PHC) settings in target districts of Pakistan.
Immediate Outcomes
Improved capacity of PHC workforce & institutions to practice, deliver and sustain WASH-enhanced MNCH services within primary HCFs.
Scope of Work
The consultant shall undertake, but not be limited to, the following tasks:
Desk Review and Mapping of Existing Policies, Practices and Frameworks
The consultant will undertake a comprehensive desk review and mapping of relevant national and provincial policies, strategies, guidelines, budgets, regulatory frameworks, institutional practices and curricula relevant to the delivery and sustainability of integrated RMNCH and WASH services. The review shall include, but not be limited to:
Provincial health strategies, plans and relevant national frameworks, including National IPC Guidelines/Frameworks;
Annual Development Plans (ADPs) and relevant budgetary allocations;
Punjab Health Care Commission (PHCC) standards and regulatory requirements applicable to primary healthcare facilities;
Existing WASH, RMNCH, MHM, IPC and gender/inclusion-related policies, protocols and operational guidelines;
Relevant departmental processes, practices and institutional mechanisms for planning, financing, implementation, monitoring and sustaining WASH and RMNCH services;
Existing academic, professional and in-service training curricula relevant to RMNCH, WASH, MHM and IPC; and
Relevant assessments, studies and materials developed or commissioned by WaterAid Pakistan and other relevant stakeholders.
Stakeholder Consultations and Key Informant Interviews
The consultant will undertake consultations with relevant provincial and district-level stakeholders to understand the practical application of existing policies and identify institutional and operational barriers. This will include:
Development of structured Key Informant Interview (KII) guides and stakeholder consultation matrices;
KIIs with relevant departments and institutions, including P&SHC, DG Health Services, DG M&E/Training, Planning & Development Department, Public Health Engineering Department (PHED), RMNCH Programme and other relevant entities;
Consultations with selected stakeholders responsible for WASH, IPC, RMNCH, MHM, health infrastructure, training and service quality; and
Any additional consultations considered necessary based on findings emerging during the assignment.
Development of Training Needs Assessment TNA Tool and Methodology
The consultant will develop a context-specific Training Needs Assessment methodology and assessment tool to systematically assess the knowledge, awareness, practices and capacity of relevant healthcare staff at the selected PHC facilities. The TNA methodology and tool shall be aligned with the objectives of the SWISH project and relevant national and provincial standards and frameworks. The consultant shall:
Develop a TNA framework covering WASH, RMNCH, MHM, IPC, GEDSI and climate resilience.
Define key assessment domains, indicators and competency areas for relevant staff cadres.
Develop appropriate data collection and assessment tools, including knowledge and practice checklists.
Define the methodology for staff selection, data collection, scoring and analysis.
Pilot/refine the tools, as required, and finalize them in consultation with IHHN and WaterAid Pakistan.
Submit the methodology and tools for technical review and approval before field-level assessment.
Training Needs Assessment (TNA) of Healthcare Staff
The consultant will conduct a TNA among relevant healthcare staff cadres at the selected PHC facilities to assess their current knowledge, awareness, practices and capacity related to:
Climate-resilient WASH;
Gender-responsive and inclusive WASH;
RMNCH-related WASH requirements;
Menstrual Hygiene Management (MHM); and
Infection Prevention and Control (IPC).
The TNA will identify key knowledge and practice gaps, priority capacity-building needs, relevant staff cadres and areas requiring further technical support or training. The findings will inform practical recommendations for strengthening ongoing and future capacity-building initiatives.
Policy, Institutional and Capacity Alignment Analysis
Based on the desk review, stakeholder consultations and TNA findings, the consultant will undertake an integrated analysis to:
Assess the alignment of existing policies, standards, practices and budgets with integrated RMNCH-WASH objectives;
Examine the extent to which gender, disability/inclusion and climate resilience are reflected in relevant policies and institutional practices;
Identify gaps in institutional roles, coordination mechanisms, implementation arrangements and resource allocation;
Assess gaps between existing policy provisions and their application at PHC level;
Identify capacity and training gaps among healthcare staff and link these with identified policy and implementation challenges; and
Identify opportunities for institutionalizing and scaling integrated WASH-RMNCH practices within existing provincial health systems.
Stakeholder Validation & Technical Consultation
The consultant will present the draft findings to IHHN, WaterAid Pakistan and relevant provincial stakeholders, including P&SHC, DG Health and other relevant departments, to validate the findings, obtain technical feedback and agree on priority recommendations.
The consultant shall:
Present key findings and recommendations to relevant stakeholders.
Facilitate technical discussions to validate findings and identify gaps.
Incorporate stakeholder feedback into the final assessment and recommendations.
Document agreed priority actions and recommendations for policy and capacity strengthening.
Recommendations and Integration Pathways
The consultant will translate the findings into practical and actionable recommendations for strengthening the policy, institutional, budgetary and capacity environment for integrated WASH and RMNCH programming. Recommendations should, where relevant, identify:
Priority policy and guideline revisions;
Opportunities for integration within provincial strategies, ADPs and planning/budgeting processes;
Institutional and coordination mechanisms required for sustainability;
Priority capacity-building and training interventions;
Opportunities to strengthen climate-resilient, gender-responsive and inclusive WASH practices; and
Potential pathways for institutionalizing successful SWISH approaches within the wider primary healthcare system.
Report Development, Validation and Policy Follow-up
The consultant will prepare a comprehensive draft policy review and TNA report consolidating the findings from all workstreams. The draft will be presented to IHHN, WaterAid Pakistan and relevant provincial stakeholders for review and validation.
Following validation, the consultant will:
Incorporate stakeholder feedback and finalize the report;
Conduct technical briefings with relevant departments, as required;
Develop a concise set of priority actions, recommendations and policy briefs for consideration by relevant authorities; and
Support strategic follow-up with key departments, where required, to facilitate consideration and potential integration of agreed recommendations into policy, planning, budgeting, training and institutional processes.

Introduction of PPAF
Pakistan Poverty Alleviation Fund (PPAF) is the premier apex institution dedicated to lifting the poor out of poverty through community-driven development across Pakistan. Established in February 1997 as a not-for-profit company under Section 42 of the Companies Ordinance 1984 (now Companies Act 2017), PPAF’s mission is to transform the lives of the impoverished, fostering a more equitable and prosperous Pakistan.
PPAF receives funding from the Government of Pakistan, prominent international donors, and also utilises its own resources to design and implement projects and initiatives that focus on climate-resilient infrastructure, green growth and energy, health, education, livelihoods, financial inclusion, and disaster resilience at the grassroots level. These interventions are implemented through PPAF's network of partner civil society organisations.
PPAF is committed to building and enhancing the capacity of its partner organisations to improve social mobilisation, and to promote the values of inclusion, participation, accountability, transparency, and stewardship. Through these efforts, PPAF aims to create sustainable and empowered communities, significantly contributing to the nation’s long-term development and stability.
For a complete profile, please visit our website at www.ppaf.org.pk

In response to evolving national economic priorities, complex geo-security realities, and shifting international funding landscapes, PPAF is undergoing a strategic realignment. Integrate national and provincial PCVE objectives, peace-building, and social cohesion indicators into PPAF's strategic direction, institutional planning, and field implementation frameworks.

Oversee an institutional security and safety framework to safeguard PPAF personnel, assets, partner institutions, and community operations across sensitive geographies.

job_title: Project Manager- Umerkot (Anticipated project)
job_description:
1. About the Organization
Pak Mission Society (PMS) is a national relief and development organization established to serve unreached and underprivileged communities across Pakistan. PMS operates in sectors including Disaster Response, Health, Education, Livelihood, WASH, and Youth Development, ensuring transparency, dignity, and equity in all its interventions.
2. Project Overview:
The Safe Health Project in Umerkot, Sindh (funded by Humedica e.V/BMZ) aims to ensure that communities in the catchment areas of eight (08) Basic Health Units (BHUs) across eight Union Councils of Taluka Kunri, District Umerkot, are resilient and have access to functional primary healthcare services that remain operational during and after climate-related disasters such as floods and heatwaves. The project strengthens structural and non-structural safety of BHUs, establishes functional Emergency Medical Teams (EMTs) linked to Health Emergency Operations Centres (HEOCs), builds community engagement and accountability mechanisms, and supports formal integration of DRR and primary healthcare governance in coordination with the District Health Office, DDMA, Rescue 1122, and WHO.
3. Position Overview:
The Project Manager will be responsible for project management at the field level, leading overall project cycle management including implementation, the technical component, financial management, and monitoring of the Safe Health Project in Umerkot. Working in the context of Umerkot's climate vulnerability and weak health facility resilience, the Project Manager will lead the retrofitting and upgrading of eight (08) Basic Health Units, the establishment of functional Emergency Medical Teams and Health Emergency Operations Centre linkages, and community engagement and DRR-health governance integration, ensuring continuity of essential health services during and after climate-related emergencies for target communities in Taluka Kunri, District Umerkot.
4. Key Responsibilities
4.1 Technical Role
Lead field-level implementation of the Safe Health Project, aligning all interventions with WHO-HSI (Health Safety Index) standards, WASH FIT, national/provincial health and DRR policy frameworks, donor priorities, and PMS's organizational goals.
Lead comprehensive risk and safety assessments of the eight (08) Basic Health Units (BHUs) using WHO-HSI adapted standards to grade facilities (green/yellow/red) and prioritize retrofitting and upgrade needs.
Oversee retrofitting and upgrading of the 08 BHUs to hazard-specific standards (flood, heatwave, earthquake, disease outbreak), including civil works such as solar power, generators, improved water storage/sanitation, and emergency medical supply stockpiling in line with the Sindh UHC Benefit Package.
Guide development and operationalization of facility-level safety maintenance plans (regular inspections, evacuation signage, equipment securing, continuity protocols) for each BHU.
Lead the establishment of eight (08) Emergency Medical Teams (EMTs) linked to BHUs and functioning under Health Emergency Operations Centres (HEOCs), and oversee delivery of training on disaster preparedness, mass casualty management, and Continuity of Operations Planning (COOP) for health staff.
Oversee facility-level emergency response plans (evacuation routes, triage, communication protocols) and the conduct of multi-hazard simulation drills ahead of monsoon and heatwave seasons.
Support integration of DRR and health governance components, including facility-level Disaster Risk Reduction plans, early warning systems, and formal linkages between BHU EMTs, HEOCs, and the District Disaster Management Authority (DDMA).
Ensure quality implementation through ongoing capacity building of field staff, health facility personnel, and community structures (VDCs, DRR Committees, CERTs).
4.2 Programme Management
Design and regularly update project cycle management documents, including detailed implementation plans, budget spending plan, procurement plans, risk management, stakeholder engagement and HR plans for the Safe Health Project.
Oversee execution of all project activities across the 08 target BHUs and their catchment Union Councils in Taluka Kunri, ensuring adherence to timelines, project objectives, and donor (Humedica/BMZ) requirements.
Identify risks throughout the project lifecycle (e.g., staff turnover at health facilities, delayed NOCs, retrofitting sustainability) and develop and monitor mitigation strategies in coordination with health and disaster management authorities.
Resolve conflicts among project staff, health facility personnel, and stakeholders through negotiation, mediation, and fostering a collaborative working environment.
Ensure all project deliverables, including retrofitting works, training packages, and facility plans, meet quality standards and comply with organizational, donor (Humedica/BMZ), and government requirements.
Prepare and present periodic progress reports, quarterly and annual reports, and project documentation for internal management, Humedica, and other stakeholders as per donor templates and standards.
Lead field-level response during climate-related emergencies (floods, heatwaves, disease outbreaks), ensuring rapid activation of EMTs, HEOC coordination, and continuity of essential health services at target BHUs.
4.3 Programme Financial Management
Prepare budget consumption plans and manage the project budget, ensuring optimal utilization of resources in line with PMS financial policies and donor requirements.
Ensure budget spending as per the donor guideline and agreed annual amount.
Participate in monthly budget-versus-actual (BvA) meetings and regularly update budget projections and forecasts.
Oversee procurement processes for retrofitting materials, medical equipment, emergency supply kits, and other program inputs, ensuring transparency, value for money, and efficiency.
4.4 Monitoring & Evaluation
Conduct regular and systematic field visits to the 08 BHUs and their catchment communities to assess the quality of retrofitting works, EMT/HEOC functionality, and training delivery against WHO-HSI, Sphere, and organizational/donor standards.
Support the M&E framework and data collection tools to monitor project indicators (facility safety scores, EMT establishment, training numbers, community awareness), ensuring data is disaggregated by gender, age, and location.
Document lessons learned, challenges, and best practices, and organize learning workshops, debriefing sessions, and case studies with district health and disaster management stakeholders.
Support the MEAL team in baseline/endline assessments, satisfaction surveys, and monitoring of the Complaints Response Mechanism (CRM), ensuring PSEA, protection, and accountability principles are upheld.
Adapt and refine implementation strategies based on monitoring data, facility assessment findings, and feedback from communities and health authorities, promoting a culture of continuous improvement.
4.5 Coordination / Networking / Partnership
Represent PMS in regular coordination with the District Health Officer (DHO), District Disaster Management Officer (DDMO)/DDMA, Rescue 1122, WHO, and other relevant government and humanitarian actors in Umerkot.
Support formalization of MOUs and coordination protocols between PMS, the Department of Health, and DDMA regarding operation of HEOCs and EMTs, and facilitate quarterly stakeholder meetings on project goals and objectives.
Represent the organization and the project in relevant coordination forums and support policy advocacy workshops/briefs at district and provincial level on health facility resilience and DRR-health integration.
Collaborate closely with community structures (VDCs, DRR Committees, CERTs) to integrate community feedback and beneficiary perspectives into project design and implementation.
Liaise with PMS Head Office (senior management, MEAL, Operations, Finance) to ensure alignment of field implementation with organizational systems and donor compliance requirements.
4.6 Team Management & Capacity Building
Supervise and mentor the project field team (technical/health officers, social mobilizers, and support staff) to ensure efficient and quality delivery of project activities.
Organize and support capacity-building workshops and training sessions for project staff, BHU-EMT members, and community volunteers on DRR, emergency management, and safe health facility standards.
Promote a collaborative work environment, encouraging teamwork and knowledge sharing among project staff, health facility personnel, and stakeholders.

Master's degree in Public Health, Disaster Risk Management, Development Studies, Social Sciences, or a related field.
Additional certifications in DRR, WASH, or health emergency management (e.g., WHO-HSI, WASH FIT, HEOC/EMT management) are advantageous.
5.2 Work Experience

Proven track record of managing infrastructure/retrofitting works, health facility resilience initiatives, or Emergency Medical Team/HEOC establishment.
Experience in community engagement, capacity building of health staff and community structures, and partnership development with government health and disaster management authorities.
5.3 Skills and Competencies

Understanding of DRR frameworks, Emergency Medical Team and Health Emergency Operations Centre structures, and district-level disaster management coordination mechanisms (DDMA, Rescue 1122).

job_title: PN 39 - Ongoing Recruitment: STTA - Mid Level National - Clinical AMR/AMS and Microbiology Specialist
job_description:
E4H Punjab TOR - Targeted Technical Assistance for PHC-Facing AMR Learning and Rational Antibiotic Use among Allied Health Professionals in Punjab
Programme
Evidence for Health (E4H) is a Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO)-funded programme aimed at strengthening Pakistan's healthcare system, thereby decreasing the burden of illness and saving lives. E4H (2023-2027) provides technical assistance (TA) to Punjab and also to the Federal and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) governments. The Punjab component is being implemented by Palladium along with Oxford Policy Management (OPM).
Through its flexible, embedded, and demand-driven model, E4H Punjab will support the government to achieve a resilient health system that is prepared for health emergencies, responsive to the latest evidence, and delivers equitable, quality, and efficient healthcare services. Specifically, E4H will deliver TA across three outputs:
Output 1: Strengthened integrated health security, with a focus on preparing and responding to health emergencies, including pandemics.
Output 2: Strengthened evidence-based decision-making to drive health sector performance and accountability.
Output 3: Improved implementation of Universal Health Coverage, with a focus on ending preventable deaths.
E4H-Punjab works in partnership with the Punjab Department of Health (DOH).
Terms of reference
Background
Pakistan and Punjab continue to face a significant antimicrobial resistance burden, driven by complex human health, animal health, pharmaceutical, infection prevention, regulatory and behavioural factors. In Punjab, multiple actors influence antimicrobial use, including both health departments, the Punjab Healthcare Commission (PHCC), Institute of Public Health (IPH) Lahore, provincial Drug Control structures, , professional bodies, pharmacies, PHC providers and community-facing health cadres.
E4H current AMR mandate is situated in the transition following closure of the Fleming Fund Country Grant. The TA will recognise and build on Fleming Fund-supported human-health platforms and achievements, including AMR surveillance and reporting, laboratory and microbiology capacity, stewardship and IPC linkages, data-use practices, and coordination mechanisms, while avoiding duplication and confirming the precise assets during inception.
The National Action Plan on AMR 2.0 (2025-2029), including Punjab participation in the national process and provincial priorities, will serve as the principal strategic reference for this TA. The assignment will translate relevant national priorities into an implementable provincial package and roadmap for the public and private health sectors
The support envisioned in Punjab focuses on practical learning, targeted advocacy and facility-level action. It does not attempt broad provincial AMR planning, major laboratory expansion or full-scale implementation. If UKHSA or other partners support provincial AMR planning, E4H will align with that work and avoid duplication.
The TORs frame the proposed technical assistance (TA) around a rational, value-for-money package that uses existing institutions, existing training platforms and selected technical anchors rather than creating new systems or attempting province-wide rollout.
E4H support will be practical and selective. It will map AMR assets and partner support, refine a limited PHC-facing learning package, support orientation and applied learning for Allied Health Professionals through selected institutional partners, and use one or two higher-level learning or technical sites only where needed for content validation, case material, antibiogram interpretation or stewardship examples.
Problem Statement
Punjab has several AMR-relevant initiatives and institutional actors, but practical linkage remains limited between AMR evidence, stewardship, IPC, prescribing behaviour, regulatory levers and the knowledge base of PHC-facing cadres. Current initiatives are not yet consistently connected across physician-led stewardship, prescribing accountability, AMC/AMU, microbiology and AST practices, periodic antibiograms, AWaRe-informed decisions, IPC, quality standards, MSDS oversight, dispensing, referral and patient counselling.
In addition to prescriber Physicians, who have a key role in AMR control, Allied Health Professionals (Pharmacists, Laboratory Technicians, Nurses) can support more consistent messages on rational antibiotic use, IPC, referral, counselling and basic stewardship practices, but they require a concise, context-appropriate learning module and facilitation approach linked to existing quality-of-care and regulatory systems. .
A targeted TA is needed to strengthen these connections, support selected institutions and facilities, develop provincial guidance, and establish a sustainable scale-up pathway.
Goal and Objective(s)
Goal
To strengthen provincial and facility-level AMR containment and antimicrobial stewardship in Punjab through an integrated package of learning, institutional support, technical guidance, MSDS recommendations and a sustainable roadmap aligned with NAP-AMR 2.0
Objectives
Develop and institutionalise an AMR/AMS learning package and CPD short course through IPH, with differentiated materials for priority cadres.
Integrate and disseminate WHO AWaRe classification, antibiogram use, AMC/AMU and other relevant AMR information within learning, clinical governance and quality platforms.
Strengthen physician-owned antimicrobial stewardship systems in selected teaching hospitals through baseline review, multidisciplinary teams, action plans, mentoring and progress tracking.
Develop draft provincial antimicrobial stewardship guidance for consultation, validation and formal government consideration.
Prepare recommendations for incorporating proportionate AMS oversight and verification requirements into PHCC MSDS and related quality-assurance processes.
Map partner support and institutional assets and develop a sustainable Punjab roadmap for AMR containment across public and private health sectors.
Target Groups and Technical Focus
Physicians and institutional leadership will be positioned as the principal owners of stewardship. Priority supporting cadres will be selected according to direct AMR relevance and may include pharmacists, microbiologists, culture-laboratory technologists, nurses, IPC personnel, public-health professionals, quality managers, facility supervisors and relevant trainers.
Differentiated content will include: prescriber stewardship and accountability for physicians; AMC/AMU, dispensing and AST-based stewardship advocacy for pharmacists; good microbiology practices, culture and susceptibility testing quality, facility AMR reporting and periodic antibiograms for microbiologists and culture-laboratory technologists; and focused stewardship, specimen, referral, counselling and IPC responsibilities for nurses, IPC and PHC-facing personnel.
IPC content will remain focused and proportionate because IPC is already embedded in MSDS and has received substantial post-COVID attention. The package will place greater emphasis on stewardship, prescribing behaviour, microbiology, antibiogram use, AMC/AMU, AWaRe and institutional accountability.
Strategic Approach
Contributions to health systems strengthening
The TA will strengthen PHC-facing AMR learning by refining and applying a concise module for Allied Health Professionals on rational antibiotic use, AMS, IPC, red flags and referral, patient counselling, AWaRe awareness, and safe practice within existing mandates.
One or two teaching hospitals or academic institutions may be engaged only as technical anchors for validation, case examples, antibiogram interpretation and practical learning inputs.
Alignment with other E4H TAs/investments
The TA aligns with E4H Output 1 by supporting integrated health security, IHR capacity, rational antimicrobial use, IPC and data-informed action. It complements E4H work on health security governance, quality of care, patient safety and regulatory strengthening by translating AMR priorities into practical learning for PHC-facing cadres.
The TA will build on E4H entry points with the Punjab Healthcare Commission and IPH, including possible linkages with MSDS orientation, quality standards, inspection learning tools, facility support, licensing dialogue, training and professional engagement. This TA is also aligned with the following TAs already completed during 2025-26 workplan:
Revision of Public Health Act
Health Manager’s Capacity Building on IHR
IHR Task Force Convening
Simulation exercises
Alignment with other donors
The TA will map ongoing AMR-related support in Punjab before confirming activities to avoid duplication with other partners like UKHSA, WHO, and others.. E4H support will only complement existing AMR surveillance, laboratory, IPC, quality, regulatory and stewardship investments.
Engagement with Drug Control, pharmacy actors, professional bodies and clinician or allied health forums will focus on feasible actions related to antibiotic sale, dispensing, prescribing behaviour, patient counselling and stewardship messaging, while recognising provincial responsibilities and relevant DRAP linkages.
Scope of Work and Delivery Methodology
The TA will be delivered from September 2026 to March 2027 through four linked workstreams. Delivery will combine provincial technical work, institutional co-development, facility-level support and dissemination through existing systems.
Phase 1 - Inception, mapping and baseline
Conduct institutional, partner and asset mapping and document relevant Fleming Fund-supported platforms and current partner investments.
Complete a focused baseline assessment of selected teaching hospitals and institutional systems covering AMS governance, prescribing, pharmacy, AMC/AMU, microbiology, AST, antibiogram production, IPC linkages and reporting.
Apply transparent selection criteria for priority cadres and learning sites, including AMR relevance, leadership commitment, service volume, laboratory/pharmacy functionality, data availability, public/private representation and feasibility.
Confirm the results framework, stakeholder-engagement and endorsement pathway, final workplan, scope boundaries, risks and coordination arrangements.
Phase 2 - Package, guidance and system design
Co-develop with IPH a modular CPD short course and differentiated materials for physicians and priority AMR-relevant cadres, using existing national and partner materials where suitable.
Prepare practical AWaRe, antibiogram, AMC/AMU, AST and stewardship resources, job aids, facilitator guidance, case scenarios and competency-based pre/post assessments.
Draft provincial AMS guidance defining governance, multidisciplinary team functions, prescribing review, pharmacy and laboratory roles, data review, reporting, escalation and accountability.
Review relevant PHCC MSDS provisions and develop proposed AMS additions or revisions with feasible indicators, evidence requirements and oversight options.
Agree dissemination arrangements, including trainer orientation, CPD channels and, subject to approval, publication on IPH, PHCC and relevant health-department websites.
Phase 3 - Institutional and facility implementation
Orient nominated trainers and deliver targeted learning sessions through IPH and participating institutions, with materials differentiated by cadre.
Support selected teaching hospitals to establish or strengthen physician-led multidisciplinary AMS arrangements and prepare time-bound facility action plans.
Provide technical mentoring on AWaRe-informed prescribing, pharmacy-led AMC/AMU review, AST-based decisions, good microbiology practices, periodic antibiograms and submission of reports to hospital management and laboratory leadership.
Facilitate structured review meetings to monitor action plans, barriers, enablers and early implementation evidence.
Consult public and private sector stakeholders on provincial guidance and MSDS recommendations.
Phase 4 - Validation, endorsement, dissemination and roadmap
Validate the CPD course, provincial AMS guidance, teaching-hospital action plans and PHCC MSDS recommendations through designated technical and government forums.
Submit final products through agreed institutional channels for written endorsement or approval by the competent authorities.
Prepare a costed and prioritised Punjab roadmap for AMR containment, aligned with NAP-AMR 2.0 and building on Fleming Fund-supported platforms, with actions, lead institutions, sequencing, resource implications, indicators, risks and public/private scale-up pathways.
Hand over editable products and a dissemination package to nominated government and institutional counterparts.
Sustainability: Capacity Building, Institutionalisation, and/or Transition Planning
Embedded learning and capacity support
Capacity support will focus on practical understanding of AMR, rational antibiotic use, AMS concepts relevant to PHC, IPC basics, patient counselling, referral, escalation and feedback. The purpose of this consultancy is to design and deliver a comprehensive farmer training program aimed at enhancing knowledge, skills and adoption of nutrition-sensitive, climate-smart, and sustainable agricultural practices. The consultancy will strengthen farmers’ capacity in diversified and resilient crop production through practical training on improved seed selection, soil and water management, integrated pest and soil fertility management, climate-smart agriculture techniques, vertical farming, aquaponics, hydroponics, and post-harvest handling, with a strong focus on improving household food security, nutrition outcomes, agricultural productivity, climate resilience, and income generation. The consultant will design, develop and deliver a comprehensive training program for farmers to enhance their knowledge, skills and adoption of nutrition-sensitive, climate-smart and sustainable agricultural practices. The consultant will conduct practical and participatory training sessions for farmers using adult-learning approaches, field demonstrations, group discussions, case studies, hands-on exercises, and problem-solving techniques. Nutrition-sensitive agriculture and crop diversification
Selection of improved and climate-resilient seed varieties
Soil preparation and land management
Seedbed preparation and planting techniques
Sowing methods and crop establishment
Integrated Pest Management (IPM)
Integrated Soil Fertility Management (ISFM)
Climate-Smart Agriculture (CSA) practices
Efficient water management practices
Vertical farming techniques
Aquaponics and hydroponics systems
Post-harvest handling, storage, and loss reduction

The Aga Khan Health Service, Pakistan (AKHS, P) is seeking an experienced Manager Finance for its Gilgit Baltistan region, based at Aga Khan Hospital, Gilgit, reporting to the CFO & Company Secretary.
Summary of the Role
The Manager Finance oversees financial management, financial planning, reporting, audits, treasury management and internal controls for the Gilgit Baltistan region. job_title: Hiring of Service Provider for International Conference on Poverty Eradication Day 2026
job_description:
Request for Proposals (RfP)
The Pakistan Poverty Alleviation Fund invites Technical and Financial Proposals from interested and qualified firms.
The firm will be selected in accordance with PPAF standard procurement guidelines.
Please submit hard copies of Technical and Financial Proposals in separate sealed envelopes by 14th September 2026 at the following address;
Procurement Section
Pakistan Poverty Alleviation Fund (PPAF)
Plot 14, Street 12, Mauve Area, G-8/1, Islamabad.
TERMS OF REFERENCE
Hiring of Service Provider for
International Conference on Poverty Eradication Day 2026
1. About Pakistan Poverty Alleviation Fund (PPAF)
Pakistan Poverty Alleviation Fund (PPAF) is the premier apex institution dedicated to lifting the poor out of poverty through community-driven development across Pakistan. Established in February 1997 as a not-for-profit company under Section 42 of the Companies Ordinance 1984 (now Companies Act 2017), PPAF’s mission is to transform the lives of the impoverished, fostering a more equitable and prosperous Pakistan.
PPAF design and implement projects and initiatives that focus on climate-resilient infrastructure, green growth and energy, health, education, livelihoods, financial inclusion, and disaster resilience at the grassroots level. These interventions are implemented through PPAF's network of partner civil society organisations.
PPAF is committed to building and enhancing the capacity of its partner organisations to improve social mobilisation, and to promote the values of inclusion, participation, accountability, transparency, and stewardship. Through these efforts, PPAF aims to create sustainable and empowered communities, significantly contributing to the nation’s long-term development and stability. For a complete profile, please visit our website at http://www.ppaf.org.pk
2. Background and Purpose
PPAF is convening the International Conference on Inclusive and Resilient Economic Empowerment and Growth on 13–14 October 2026 at Hotel Serena in Islamabad to mark the International Day for the Eradication of Poverty. The two-day conference attended by around 400 participants will provide a platform to reflect on progress and persistent challenges in poverty reduction, while exploring emerging pathways for inclusive, resilient and sustainable economic empowerment in Pakistan and beyond.
For nearly three decades, PPAF has worked with thousands of vulnerable and underserved rural communities across Pakistan, supporting them through community-driven and innovative approaches to address poverty in a sustainable manner. Its experience demonstrates that lasting poverty reduction requires an integrated approach that goes beyond income support to include productive assets, skills, financial access, entrepreneurship, market linkages, social protection and resilience to climate and other shocks.
Building on this experience, the conference will bring together senior government representatives, donors and development partners, national and international experts, academics, practitioners, private sector representatives, media and community voices. Discussions will focus on poverty graduation, social enterprises and SMEs, youth economic empowerment, financial inclusion, climate-aligned growth and sustainable investment, providing an opportunity to exchange evidence, experience and perspectives on advancing inclusive and resilient economic growth.
Given the scale, profile and diverse participation expected at the Conference, strategic branding, visibility and high-quality event execution will be critical to amplifying its purpose and impact. A well-conceived and professionally executed communication and visibility approach will help establish the Conference as a significant platform for policy dialogue, knowledge exchange and collaboration on poverty alleviation and inclusive economic development. Strong visual branding, high-quality event production, targeted media outreach and compelling storytelling will be essential to effectively communicate the Conference's key messages, engage diverse audiences, enhance its visibility nationally and internationally, and extend the reach and relevance of the discussions beyond the two-day event.
The Service Provider will therefore be expected to provide integrated branding, event visibility, media engagement, content and storytelling support to ensure a cohesive, high-quality and impactful Conference experience, while helping sustain visibility and engagement around the outcomes and recommendations emerging from the Conference. The discussions will culminate in a Conference Communiqué capturing key recommendations and a way forward.
3. Objectives
The assignment will aim to:
Position PPAF as a leading national voice and thought leader on poverty alleviation.
Showcase evidence, experience, innovation and lessons from PPAF and other national and international actors to inform dialogue on poverty alleviation.
Generate strong national and digital media visibility for the conference and PPAF.
Strengthen engagement and confidence among government, donors and development partners in PPAF's knowledge, institutional and implementation capabilities.
4. Scope of Work
The Service Provider will lead the creative, communication, event management, production coordination, media/PR, digital campaign and conference documentation components of the assignment. The Service Provider will also coordinate and monitor the delivery and installation of approved conference materials and specialised production requirements, ensuring compliance with agreed specifications, timelines and quality standards.
The Service Provider will be responsible for developing the required specifications, designs, production briefs and schedules, coordinating with designated suppliers, monitoring delivery and installation, and ensuring compliance with approved specifications, timelines and quality standards.
A. PRE-CONFERENCE: DESIGN, PREPARATION AND CAMPAIGN
The Service Provider will lead the creative, communication, event management, production coordination and operational preparation of the conference, including management of suppliers engaged for these activities. It will prepare recommendations and materials for PPAF review and approval and will manage implementation once approved.
The Service Provider will provide the following services
Develop the conference creative concept, logo, themes, key messages, visual treatment and communication narrative, aligned with the PPAF conference theme and approved visual direction.
Review and refine the conference programme and recommend engaging session formats, including plenaries, expert conversations, community voices and parallel sessions.
Develop session themes, briefs and discussion questions; prepare tailored talking points and key messages for speakers in the plenary and closing sessions; and support speaker briefing to ensure alignment with the Conference objectives, themes and key messages.
Suggest and finalise the guest list in consultation with PPAF, extend invitations, manage RSVPs, and secure final confirmations to ensure attendance.
Design invitations, programme, badges, folders, signage, stage graphics, digital screen content and other conference materials.
Recommend appropriate conference giveaways, including shields and other visibility materials, and oversee their aesthetics, design and branding as required
Develop the event production and operational plan covering stage, audience seating, AV, screens, registration, branding, staffing and venue requirements.
Design concepts and manage artwork for conference exhibition stalls/pavilions and other approved visibility installations.
Coordinate the production, printing and installation of approved conference materials and visibility materials, in coordination with designated suppliers and in accordance with approved specifications, timelines and quality standards.
Coordinate and monitor relevant event production and other suppliers to ensure timely delivery, installation and quality of approved requirements.
Develop a Conference Communication Plan covering pre-conference, during-conference and post-conference communication objectives, audiences, messages, channels, content, media engagement, digital activity and reporting.
Develop an outdoor promotion plan for the Conference, identifying appropriate locations and formats for banners, billboards and digital displays on roads and highways in proximity to the conference venue, subject to PPAF approval.
Coordinate and manage the required approvals and permissions from relevant authorities for outdoor promotional placements, and oversee the design, production, installation and timely removal of approved outdoor visibility materials.
Prepare the conference information kit, media kit, key messages, press advisories/templates, speaker and conference profiles, and other approved promotional content.
Initiate media and stakeholder engagement in advance of the conference and identify appropriate public/partner engagement opportunities, subject to timing and approval.
Provide strategic advisory and value-addition support on emerging and unforeseen requirements throughout the assignment, including identification of new opportunities, risks and emerging trends; recommendations for innovative approaches beyond the agreed scope of activities; timely advice and adaptive support in response to changing Conference requirements; and post-conference lessons learned and recommendations to inform future PPAF events.
B. CONFERENCE DELIVERY: EVENT MANAGEMENT AND DOCUMENTATION
The Service Provider will provide full professional management of the two-day conference, including:
Overall event coordination and on-site management, including management of any approved outdoor promotion and visibility requirements during the Conference.
Event coordination throughout the two-day conference, including registration, ushering, MC/moderator support, participant-facing arrangements and media desk management.
Stage, session and technical management, including coordination of AV, lighting, sound, digital screens, presentations and session flow.
Coordination and supervision of suppliers during venue setup and conference delivery, including verification of branding, décor, visibility, exhibition/stall installations and technical requirements against approved specifications.
On-site media coordination and journalist support, including facilitation of media access to designated speakers and organisational representatives.
Professional photography and video documentation of the conference.
Livestreaming and real-time digital/social media coverage, as approved under the communication plan.
Speaker, panellist and participant interviews/testimonials and short-form video content, with the organisation facilitating access to designated spokespersons and participants.
Daily conference highlights, photographs, videos and reels for approved dissemination.
Press releases and conference news content, based on approved institutional messaging and conference proceedings.
Real-time monitoring and resolution of production or supplier-related issues, in coordination with the organisation and relevant suppliers.
C. MEDIA, PR AND ADVOCACY: BEFORE, DURING AND AFTER
The Service Provider will deliver:
Professionally edited 2–3-minute conference film/event highlights video, incorporating approved footage and messaging.
Edited and curated photographic documentation of the conference.
Post-conference media and digital campaign, including dissemination of key conference messages, findings and outcomes through agreed channels.
Thought leadership and feature content, including opinion pieces, expert commentary, human-interest stories and other appropriate content, based on substantive inputs and approvals from the organisation.
Conference highlights and key recommendations presented in appropriate communication/knowledge formats.
Comprehensive Conference Report, covering the executive summary, proceedings, thematic sessions, panel discussions, Q&A, key takeaways, findings, recommendations and other agreed outcomes, based on session documentation and substantive inputs provided/validated by the organisation.
Media and communications performance report, including media coverage, insertions, platforms, reach and comprehensive social media/digital analytics.
Consolidated conference documentation archive, including photographs, videos, communication materials and other agreed outputs.

job_title: PN 39 - Ongoing Recruitment: STTA - Junior Level National - Research Associate
job_description:
E4H Punjab TOR - Targeted Technical Assistance for PHC-Facing AMR Learning and Rational Antibiotic Use among Allied Health Professionals in Punjab
Programme
Evidence for Health (E4H) is a Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO)-funded programme aimed at strengthening Pakistan's healthcare system, thereby decreasing the burden of illness and saving lives. E4H (2023-2027) provides technical assistance (TA) to Punjab and also to the Federal and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) governments. The Punjab component is being implemented by Palladium along with Oxford Policy Management (OPM).
Through its flexible, embedded, and demand-driven model, E4H Punjab will support the government to achieve a resilient health system that is prepared for health emergencies, responsive to the latest evidence, and delivers equitable, quality, and efficient healthcare services. Specifically, E4H will deliver TA across three outputs:
Output 1: Strengthened integrated health security, with a focus on preparing and responding to health emergencies, including pandemics.
Output 2: Strengthened evidence-based decision-making to drive health sector performance and accountability.
Output 3: Improved implementation of Universal Health Coverage, with a focus on ending preventable deaths.
E4H-Punjab works in partnership with the Punjab Department of Health (DOH).
Terms of reference
Background
Pakistan and Punjab continue to face a significant antimicrobial resistance burden, driven by complex human health, animal health, pharmaceutical, infection prevention, regulatory and behavioural factors. In Punjab, multiple actors influence antimicrobial use, including both health departments, the Punjab Healthcare Commission (PHCC), Institute of Public Health (IPH) Lahore, provincial Drug Control structures, , professional bodies, pharmacies, PHC providers and community-facing health cadres.
E4H current AMR mandate is situated in the transition following closure of the Fleming Fund Country Grant. The TA will recognise and build on Fleming Fund-supported human-health platforms and achievements, including AMR surveillance and reporting, laboratory and microbiology capacity, stewardship and IPC linkages, data-use practices, and coordination mechanisms, while avoiding duplication and confirming the precise assets during inception.
The National Action Plan on AMR 2.0 (2025-2029), including Punjab participation in the national process and provincial priorities, will serve as the principal strategic reference for this TA. The assignment will translate relevant national priorities into an implementable provincial package and roadmap for the public and private health sectors
The support envisioned in Punjab focuses on practical learning, targeted advocacy and facility-level action. It does not attempt broad provincial AMR planning, major laboratory expansion or full-scale implementation. If UKHSA or other partners support provincial AMR planning, E4H will align with that work and avoid duplication.
The TORs frame the proposed technical assistance (TA) around a rational, value-for-money package that uses existing institutions, existing training platforms and selected technical anchors rather than creating new systems or attempting province-wide rollout.
E4H support will be practical and selective. It will map AMR assets and partner support, refine a limited PHC-facing learning package, support orientation and applied learning for Allied Health Professionals through selected institutional partners, and use one or two higher-level learning or technical sites only where needed for content validation, case material, antibiogram interpretation or stewardship examples.
Problem Statement
Punjab has several AMR-relevant initiatives and institutional actors, but practical linkage remains limited between AMR evidence, stewardship, IPC, prescribing behaviour, regulatory levers and the knowledge base of PHC-facing cadres. Current initiatives are not yet consistently connected across physician-led stewardship, prescribing accountability, AMC/AMU, microbiology and AST practices, periodic antibiograms, AWaRe-informed decisions, IPC, quality standards, MSDS oversight, dispensing, referral and patient counselling.
In addition to prescriber Physicians, who have a key role in AMR control, Allied Health Professionals (Pharmacists, Laboratory Technicians, Nurses) can support more consistent messages on rational antibiotic use, IPC, referral, counselling and basic stewardship practices, but they require a concise, context-appropriate learning module and facilitation approach linked to existing quality-of-care and regulatory systems. .
A targeted TA is needed to strengthen these connections, support selected institutions and facilities, develop provincial guidance, and establish a sustainable scale-up pathway.
Goal and Objective(s)
Goal
To strengthen provincial and facility-level AMR containment and antimicrobial stewardship in Punjab through an integrated package of learning, institutional support, technical guidance, MSDS recommendations and a sustainable roadmap aligned with NAP-AMR 2.0
Objectives
Develop and institutionalise an AMR/AMS learning package and CPD short course through IPH, with differentiated materials for priority cadres.
Integrate and disseminate WHO AWaRe classification, antibiogram use, AMC/AMU and other relevant AMR information within learning, clinical governance and quality platforms.
Strengthen physician-owned antimicrobial stewardship systems in selected teaching hospitals through baseline review, multidisciplinary teams, action plans, mentoring and progress tracking.
Develop draft provincial antimicrobial stewardship guidance for consultation, validation and formal government consideration.
Prepare recommendations for incorporating proportionate AMS oversight and verification requirements into PHCC MSDS and related quality-assurance processes.
Map partner support and institutional assets and develop a sustainable Punjab roadmap for AMR containment across public and private health sectors.
Target Groups and Technical Focus
Physicians and institutional leadership will be positioned as the principal owners of stewardship. Priority supporting cadres will be selected according to direct AMR relevance and may include pharmacists, microbiologists, culture-laboratory technologists, nurses, IPC personnel, public-health professionals, quality managers, facility supervisors and relevant trainers.
Differentiated content will include: prescriber stewardship and accountability for physicians; AMC/AMU, dispensing and AST-based stewardship advocacy for pharmacists; good microbiology practices, culture and susceptibility testing quality, facility AMR reporting and periodic antibiograms for microbiologists and culture-laboratory technologists; and focused stewardship, specimen, referral, counselling and IPC responsibilities for nurses, IPC and PHC-facing personnel.
IPC content will remain focused and proportionate because IPC is already embedded in MSDS and has received substantial post-COVID attention. The package will place greater emphasis on stewardship, prescribing behaviour, microbiology, antibiogram use, AMC/AMU, AWaRe and institutional accountability.
Strategic Approach
Contributions to health systems strengthening
The TA will strengthen PHC-facing AMR learning by refining and applying a concise module for Allied Health Professionals on rational antibiotic use, AMS, IPC, red flags and referral, patient counselling, AWaRe awareness, and safe practice within existing mandates.
One or two teaching hospitals or academic institutions may be engaged only as technical anchors for validation, case examples, antibiogram interpretation and practical learning inputs.
Alignment with other E4H TAs/investments
The TA aligns with E4H Output 1 by supporting integrated health security, IHR capacity, rational antimicrobial use, IPC and data-informed action. It complements E4H work on health security governance, quality of care, patient safety and regulatory strengthening by translating AMR priorities into practical learning for PHC-facing cadres.
The TA will build on E4H entry points with the Punjab Healthcare Commission and IPH, including possible linkages with MSDS orientation, quality standards, inspection learning tools, facility support, licensing dialogue, training and professional engagement. This TA is also aligned with the following TAs already completed during 2025-26 workplan:
Revision of Public Health Act
Health Manager’s Capacity Building on IHR
IHR Task Force Convening
Simulation exercises
Alignment with other donors
The TA will map ongoing AMR-related support in Punjab before confirming activities to avoid duplication with other partners like UKHSA, WHO, and others.. E4H support will only complement existing AMR surveillance, laboratory, IPC, quality, regulatory and stewardship investments.
Engagement with Drug Control, pharmacy actors, professional bodies and clinician or allied health forums will focus on feasible actions related to antibiotic sale, dispensing, prescribing behaviour, patient counselling and stewardship messaging, while recognising provincial responsibilities and relevant DRAP linkages.
Scope of Work and Delivery Methodology
The TA will be delivered from September 2026 to March 2027 through four linked workstreams. Delivery will combine provincial technical work, institutional co-development, facility-level support and dissemination through existing systems.
Phase 1 - Inception, mapping and baseline
Conduct institutional, partner and asset mapping and document relevant Fleming Fund-supported platforms and current partner investments.
Complete a focused baseline assessment of selected teaching hospitals and institutional systems covering AMS governance, prescribing, pharmacy, AMC/AMU, microbiology, AST, antibiogram production, IPC linkages and reporting.
Apply transparent selection criteria for priority cadres and learning sites, including AMR relevance, leadership commitment, service volume, laboratory/pharmacy functionality, data availability, public/private representation and feasibility.
Confirm the results framework, stakeholder-engagement and endorsement pathway, final workplan, scope boundaries, risks and coordination arrangements.
Phase 2 - Package, guidance and system design
Co-develop with IPH a modular CPD short course and differentiated materials for physicians and priority AMR-relevant cadres, using existing national and partner materials where suitable.
Prepare practical AWaRe, antibiogram, AMC/AMU, AST and stewardship resources, job aids, facilitator guidance, case scenarios and competency-based pre/post assessments.
Draft provincial AMS guidance defining governance, multidisciplinary team functions, prescribing review, pharmacy and laboratory roles, data review, reporting, escalation and accountability.
Review relevant PHCC MSDS provisions and develop proposed AMS additions or revisions with feasible indicators, evidence requirements and oversight options.
Agree dissemination arrangements, including trainer orientation, CPD channels and, subject to approval, publication on IPH, PHCC and relevant health-department websites.
Phase 3 - Institutional and facility implementation
Orient nominated trainers and deliver targeted learning sessions through IPH and participating institutions, with materials differentiated by cadre.
Support selected teaching hospitals to establish or strengthen physician-led multidisciplinary AMS arrangements and prepare time-bound facility action plans.
Provide technical mentoring on AWaRe-informed prescribing, pharmacy-led AMC/AMU review, AST-based decisions, good microbiology practices, periodic antibiograms and submission of reports to hospital management and laboratory leadership.
Facilitate structured review meetings to monitor action plans, barriers, enablers and early implementation evidence.
Consult public and private sector stakeholders on provincial guidance and MSDS recommendations.
Phase 4 - Validation, endorsement, dissemination and roadmap
Validate the CPD course, provincial AMS guidance, teaching-hospital action plans and PHCC MSDS recommendations through designated technical and government forums.
Submit final products through agreed institutional channels for written endorsement or approval by the competent authorities.
Prepare a costed and prioritised Punjab roadmap for AMR containment, aligned with NAP-AMR 2.0 and building on Fleming Fund-supported platforms, with actions, lead institutions, sequencing, resource implications, indicators, risks and public/private scale-up pathways.
Hand over editable products and a dissemination package to nominated government and institutional counterparts.
Sustainability: Capacity Building, Institutionalisation, and/or Transition Planning
Embedded learning and capacity support
Capacity support will focus on practical understanding of AMR, rational antibiotic use, AMS concepts relevant to PHC, IPC basics, patient counselling, referral, escalation and feedback. The package will be suitable for Allied Health Professionals, supervisors, trainers or institutional focal persons.
Institutionalisation through existing systems
The TA will explore how module materials and learning can be linked with PHCC quality standards, MSDS-related orientation, IPH training channels, Drug Control dialogue, CPD platforms, supervisory routines, facility support tools and patient safety or quality improvement mechanisms.
Transition and handover

Simulation exercises

Description
The Better Cotton Initiative (BCI) is the world’s largest cotton sustainability programme. Our mission: to help cotton communities survive and thrive, while protecting and restoring the environment. Through our network of field-level partners we have provided training on sustainable farming practices to more than 2.9 million cotton farmers in 26 countries. More than a fifth of the world’s cotton is now grown under the BCI Standard and our membership network includes more than 2,400 members.
Better Cotton Initiative, Pakistan (BCI Pakistan) is registered in Pakistan and working under a collaboration/service agreement with Better Cotton Initiative, Global.
More information about BCI can be found on our website: www.bettercotton.org
Background
This process will be used to select consultants to conduct the Due Diligence of potential programme partners (PP) in Pakistan over the coming years.
The purpose of the Due Diligence process is to help BCI to ensure that the PPs we work with, or fund, have adequate governance structures, policies, and operational systems in place. It can also help organisations ensure they observe both international and domestic law and build towards the requirements of corporate Due Diligence.
The Due Diligence framework aims to reduce partnership risks for BCI and also supports PPs by implementing a remediation plan to enable them to comply with BCI’s requirements, strengthen their organisation and ensure a long-term partnership.
Due Diligence is an on-going, proactive, and reactive process through which PPs can identify, prevent, mitigate, and account for how they address actual and potential adverse impacts as an integral part of decision-making and risk management systems.
BCI’s due diligence covers seven areas: ethics, governance, HR, environment and operations, financial stability and governance, and where applicable - downstream local partners.
The due diligence is structured around:
Assessing the organisation and its undertakings to identify the factual circumstances under which the business is operating.
Identifying and assessing any actual or potential risks by evaluating the factual circumstances against recognised standards.
Preventing or mitigating the identified risks by adopting and implementing a corrective risk action plan.
Scope of Work
The objective of the consultancy is to conduct the Due Diligence process in Pakistan with one (1) existing PP, in accordance with BCI’s guidelines.
Through direct relationships with the PP, the consultant will be responsible for undertaking the entire Due Diligence process with the support of BCI’s team. In addition to skills, competencies and expertise, we will consider value for money and demonstrable commitment to the sustainability field to evaluate applications.
